# Overview

The purpose of this wiki page is to provide a high-level technical overview of the `gene-perturbation-prediction` codebase. The repository investigates context-conditioned single-gene dependency prediction (`GeneEffect`) and synthetic-lethality (SL) ranking in held-out cancer cell lines [README.md:3-5](). 

For deep technical details, configuration specifications, and experimental protocols, refer to the child pages:
- [Getting Started and Environment](#1.1) — uv/pyproject setup, dependencies (`torch`, `arc-state`, `scanpy`), running tests, and HPC `run.sh` entrypoints.
- [Research Contract and Documentation Vault](#1.2) — `docs/` hierarchy: blueprint authority, specs, protocols, results; agent instruction files (`CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`).
- [Scientific Protocols and Benchmarks](#1.3) — GeneEffect residual protocol, SL ranking protocol, 226-cell-line split, DepMap 26Q1 and perturb-seq datasets.

---

## 1. Research Goal and Core Framing

The central research question is whether a virtual cell model trained on single-cell perturbation responses can predict how a gene's fitness cost (GeneEffect) shifts across distinct cellular contexts, enabling robust synthetic-lethal ranking in cell lines excluded from all fitting steps [README.md:27-31]().

Key architectural and scientific boundaries include:
- **Generalization Axis**: Generalization targets **held-out cell lines**, not held-out genes [docs/01-blueprint.md:10-15]().
- **No External Graphs**: No synthetic-lethality graph or interaction network enters the feature extraction or prediction path [docs/01-blueprint.md:15-16]().
- **Internal Baselines**: Models must outperform context-blind gene means, null baselines, and context-ablated heads before any biological context claim is considered [README.md:31-32]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    sub-natural["Natural Language Space"]
    "ResearchGoal" --> "ContextConditionedGeneEffect"
    "ResearchGoal" --> "SyntheticLethalityRanking"
    
    sub-code["Code Entity Space"]
    "ContextConditionedGeneEffect" --> src_experiments_geneeffect["src/experiments/geneeffect.py"]
    "SyntheticLethalityRanking" --> src_baselines["src/baselines/"]
    src_experiments_geneeffect --> src_training_trainer["src/training/trainer.py"]
    src_training_trainer --> src_model["src/model/"]
```

**Sources:** [README.md:1-49](), [docs/01-blueprint.md:1-33]()

---

## 2. Repository Layout and Module Architecture

The repository separates input caching, neural network modules, optimization loops, evaluation, and experiment orchestration into dedicated subpackages under `src/` [CLAUDE.md:52-55]().

| Directory | Role and Modules |
| --- | --- |
| `src/data/` | Data loaders, dataset definitions, split verification (`src/data/splits.py`), and raw ingestion builders (`src/data/prepare/`) [CLAUDE.md:52-67](). |
| `src/model/` | Neural network components: STATE adapters (`src/model/state.py`), ESM2 perturbation adapters (`src/model/adapter.py`), and the five-block residual head (`src/model/head.py`) [CLAUDE.md:56-59](). |
| `src/training/` | Optimization loops (`src/training/trainer.py`), Huber loss, response replay sampling (`src/training/sampling.py`), and checkpointing [CLAUDE.md:56-59](). |
| `src/eval/` | Evaluation scripts and metric calculators for GeneEffect and response distributions (`src/eval/geneeffect.py`, `src/eval/response.py`) [CLAUDE.md:60-62](). |
| `src/baselines/` | Baseline control implementations (gene-mean, copy-prior, nearest-line, context-PCA-ridge) [CLAUDE.md:62](). |
| `src/experiments/` | End-to-end command-line wiring for preparation, training, and baselines (`src/experiments/prepare.py`, `src/experiments/geneeffect.py`) [CLAUDE.md:53-56](). |
| `configs/` | YAML configuration files (`configs/geneeffect_joint.yaml`) and benchmark split manifests (`configs/benchmarks/`) [CLAUDE.md:68-71](). |
| `hpc/` | High-performance computing execution scripts (`hpc/run.sh`) and multi-GPU orchestration [CLAUDE.md:30-36](). |

```mermaid
graph TD
    Config["configs/geneeffect_joint.yaml"] --> Prep["src/experiments/prepare.py"]
    Prep --> Caches["data/geneeffect_joint/v1/ (Immutable Caches)"]
    Caches --> Train["src/train.py"]
    Train --> Trainer["src/training/trainer.py"]
    Trainer --> Model["src/model/ (STATE + ESM2 + Head)"]
    Model --> Eval["src/evaluate.py"]
    Eval --> Metrics["outputs/evaluation/"]
```

**Sources:** [CLAUDE.md:50-72](), [AGENTS.md:10-18]()

---

## 3. The Prepare → Train → Evaluate Lifecycle

The execution lifecycle is strictly sequential and governed by a single YAML configuration [CLAUDE.md:51-61]():

1. **Preparation (`src/experiments/prepare.py`)**: Builds immutable input caches under `prepared_root` (`data/geneeffect_joint/v1`), including Tx1 basal-embedding caches, q_sc caches, ESM2 protein feature tables, and response bags. **Training opens these caches and never rebuilds them** [CLAUDE.md:53-55]().
2. **Training (`src/train.py` / `src/training/trainer.py`)**: Executes joint optimization. Every training update minimizes GeneEffect Huber loss, while every fourth update replays response reconstruction across four anchor cell lines [CLAUDE.md:56-59](). Early stopping and checkpoint selection (`best.pt`) rely **exclusively** on validation GeneEffect loss (`val_geneeffect_loss`) [CLAUDE.md:58-59]().
3. **Evaluation (`src/evaluate.py`)**: Restores fitted preprocessing from the checkpoint and exports performance metrics, predictions (`predictions.parquet`), and per-gene/per-line breakdowns [CLAUDE.md:60-62]().

**Sources:** [CLAUDE.md:51-62](), [docs/01-blueprint.md:75-99]()

---

# Page: Getting Started and Environment

# Getting Started and Environment

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [hpc/run.sh](hpc/run.sh)
- [pyproject.toml](pyproject.toml)
- [tests/conftest.py](tests/conftest.py)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope
This page details the local and high-performance computing (HPC) environment configuration for the `gene-perturbation-prediction` repository. It covers dependency management via `uv` and `pyproject.toml`, core library versions (`torch`, `arc-state`, `scanpy`), environment hardening and test suites via `tests/conftest.py`, and cluster execution orchestration through `hpc/run.sh`. 

---

## 1. Project Initialization and Dependency Management

The project uses `uv` for fast dependency resolution and environment bootstrapping, pinned to Python `>=3.11,<3.13` [pyproject.toml:5-11](). Project metadata and dependencies are declared in `pyproject.toml` [pyproject.toml:5-31](), with strict locking handled in `uv.lock` [uv.lock:1-3]().

The core dependency stack includes scientific computing libraries, deep learning frameworks, and domain-specific single-cell analysis tools:
- **Deep Learning & Acceleration**: `torch>=2.7.0`, `accelerate>=1.13.0`, and the external perturbation backbone `arc-state` loaded directly via Git reference (`@git+https://github.1com/ArcInstitute/state.git@bf4fbc9ea35bf4d1e91afe201b663dec5d8bdd48`) [pyproject.toml:12-14,27]().
- **Single-Cell & Bioinformatics**: `scanpy>=1.11.2`, `anndata>=0.12.10`, `mudata>=0.3.8`, and `scvi-tools>=1.4.0.post1,<1.4.1` [pyproject.toml:13,16,22,24]().
- **Data & Numerical Backends**: `numpy>=2.2.6`, `pandas>=2.2.3`, `scipy>=1.15.0`, `h5py==3.15.1`, and `pyarrow>=14.0.2` [pyproject.toml:15,18-20,25]().

Optional dependencies are partitioned into distinct installation groups:
- `baseline`: Includes `xgboost==2.1.4` for tree-based control models [pyproject.toml:33-36]().
- `research`: Includes `datasets>=2.10.0` and `scib>=1.1.0` for integration benchmarking [pyproject.toml:37-40]().
- `viz`: Includes visualization libraries such as `matplotlib==3.10.7`, `seaborn==0.13.2`, `networkx==3.5`, and `tabulate==0.9.0` [pyproject.toml:41-46]().
- `dev`: Development group containing `pytest>=8.3.5`, `ruff>=0.11.8`, and `ipython>=8.18.1` [pyproject.toml:48-55]().

```mermaid
title "Dependency and Configuration Architecture"
graph TD
    subgraph "PyProjectConfig [pyproject.toml]"
        A[pyproject.toml] --> B[CoreDependencies]
        A --> C[OptionalGroups]
        A --> D[DevGroup]
        A --> E[ToolConfigRuffPytest]
    end
    subgraph "Core Stack"
        B --> F[torch]
        B --> G[arc-state]
        B --> H[scanpy]
        B --> I[anndata]
    end
    subgraph "Tooling"
        E --> J[pytest]
        E --> K[ruff]
    end
    classDef default fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px;
```
*Sources: [pyproject.toml:1-101](), [uv.lock:1-7]()*.

---

## 2. Test Environment and Conftest Guards

The test suite is located in `tests/` and executed using `pytest`, configured under `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` [pyproject.toml:99-101](). To prevent platform-specific crashes, race conditions, and backend incompatibilities, `tests/conftest.py` executes critical environment initialization before any test modules or external libraries are loaded [tests/conftest.py:1-30]().

### Key Environment Guards
1. **MPS Fallback Guard**: Sets `PYTORCH_ENABLE_MPS_FALLBACK=1` to allow operations lacking native Apple Silicon MPS backward implementations (such as specific distance metrics or energy distance losses relying on `torch.cdist`) to seamlessly fall back to CPU execution [tests/conftest.py:7-12]().
2. **OpenMP Thread-Pool Pinning**: Sets `OMP_NUM_THREADS=1` to prevent segmentation faults caused by conflicting OpenMP runtimes bundled independently in `scipy` (sparse matrix conversions) and `torch` (sparse tensor construction) [tests/conftest.py:14-19]().
3. **OpenMP Load-Order Guard**: Safely imports `xgboost` prior to `torch` loading to establish a stable dynamic library load order on macOS, avoiding inter-library conflicts [tests/conftest.py:21-29]().

```mermaid
title "Conftest Environment Initialization Flow"
graph TD
    subgraph "Test Execution Entry [tests/conftest.py]"
        Start[pytest initialization] --> MPS[Set PYTORCH_ENABLE_MPS_FALLBACK=1]
        MPS --> OMP[Set OMP_NUM_THREADS=1]
        OMP --> XGB[Import xgboost to pin libomp load order]
        XGB --> Fixtures[Register Synthetic Fixtures: synthetic_benchmark_csv, synthetic_bags_npz]
    end
    classDef default fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px;
```
*Sources: [tests/conftest.py:1-155]()*.

---

## 3. HPC Execution Entrypoints (`hpc/run.sh`)

Cluster execution and script orchestration are managed through the shell script `hpc/run.sh` [hpc/run.sh:1-45](). The script standardizes environment paths, validates visible accelerator devices, and handles distributed training launches via Hugging Face `accelerate`.

### Supported Subcommands
- `prepare`: Invokes data preparation modules via `src.experiments.prepare` [hpc/run.sh:6,32]().
- `train`: Dynamically counts available CUDA devices, configures multi-GPU training flags, and launches `src.train` through `accelerate` [hpc/run.sh:7,34-43]().
- `test`: Evaluates a saved checkpoint using `src.evaluate` [hpc/run.sh:8,33]().
- `p1a`, `p1b`, `p1c`: Dispatches diagnostic experiment programs for response-pathway analysis (`src.experiments.p1a`, `src.experiments.p1b`, `src.experiments.p1c`) [hpc/run.sh:9-11,29-31]().

```mermaid
title "HPC Script Command Dispatch and Execution"
graph TD
    subgraph "HPC Entrypoint [hpc/run.sh]"
        CLI[hpc/run.sh command args] --> Switch{Command Type}
        Switch -->|prepare| Prep[Exec python -m src.experiments.prepare]
        Switch -->|train| TrainCheck[Check torch.cuda.device_count]
        TrainCheck -->|Workers > 1| MultiGPU[Launch accelerate multi_gpu bf16]
        TrainCheck -->|Workers <= 1| SingleGPU[Launch accelerate single GPU bf16]
        Switch -->|test| TestEval[Exec python -m src.evaluate]
        Switch -->|p1a/p1b/p1c| ExpDispatch[Exec python -m src.experiments.p1a/b/c]
    end
    classDef default fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px;
```
*Sources: [hpc/run.sh:1-45]()*.

---

## 4. Summary of Verification Commands

To verify the local installation and test setup, run the following commands:

| Operation | Command | Target / Module |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Environment Sync** | `uv sync` | Bootstraps `.venv` from `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` |
| **Test Suite** | `uv run pytest` | Executes all unit and integration tests under `tests/` |
| **Data Preparation** | `./hpc/run.sh prepare configs/geneeffect_joint.yaml` | Executes pipeline preparation entrypoint [hpc/run.sh:6]() |
| **Distributed Training** | `./hpc/run.sh train configs/geneeffect_joint.yaml` | Dispatches multi-GPU training via Accelerate [hpc/run.sh:7]() |

*Sources: [pyproject.toml:57-58](), [hpc/run.sh:1-45](), [tests/conftest.py:1-31]()*.

### Purpose and Scope

This page documents the structural design, governance rules, and documentation hierarchy of the `docs/` vault and agent instruction infrastructure (`CLAUDE.md`, `.codex/`, `.claude/skills/`). In this codebase, written documentation serves as the binding authority: if code and the vault disagree, the vault wins and the code is treated as a bug [.claude/skills/research-vault/SKILL.md:6-9](). This page details the blueprint hierarchy, execution protocols, specification paths, empirical results registries, and multi-agent coordination systems.

---

## 1. Authority Ordering and Vault Hierarchy

The `docs/` hierarchy implements a strict authority ordering. Lower-level documents specify how higher-level blueprints are made executable, but they never relax or contradict the higher-level claims [.claude/skills/research-vault/SKILL.md:11-25]().

```
01-blueprint.md              contract + claim bars   (frozen)
  > 02-literature-review.md  related work, novelty boundary
    > 03-geneeffect-protocol.md  the implemented GeneEffect track, executable
      > 04-sl-ranking-protocol.md  the SL-pair protocol built on it
        > docs/specs/*.md        tracked designs, incl. the Exp13 GeneEffect residual spec
          > docs/results/*.md    evidence
```

- **`docs/01-blueprint.md`**: Defines the central research task, generalization boundaries (cell-line holdout vs gene holdout), math for the GeneEffect residual protocol, and claim boundaries [docs/01-blueprint.md:1-126](). It is permanently frozen [docs/01-blueprint.md:95-100]().
- **`docs/02-literature-review.md`**: Surveys related work, contextualizing model choices against prior art without introducing external novelty claims [docs/02-literature-review.md:1-111]().
- **`docs/03-geneeffect-protocol.md`**: The executable specification for the GeneEffect track, detailing input tensors, data splits, and model architectures [docs/03-geneeffect-protocol.md:1-130]().
- **`docs/specs/*.md`**: Engineering specifications and historical staged protocols, such as the Exp13 GeneEffect residual benchmark specification [docs/specs/2026-08-17-exp13-geneeffect-residual-protocol.md:1-102]().
- **`docs/results/*.md`**: Immutable evidentiary artifacts recording completed experiment outcomes, manifests, and comparative metrics [docs/results/p1_response_pathway_diagnostics/README.md:1-109]().

### Diagram: Natural Language Space to Code Entity Space (Blueprint & Protocols)

```mermaid
graph TD
  BP["docs/01-blueprint.md"] -->|Defines Task & Huber Objective| SrcTrain["src/train.py"]
  GEProto["docs/03-geneeffect-protocol.md"] -->|Specifies Evaluation Splits| EvalGE["src/eval/geneeffect.py"]
  ExpSpec["docs/specs/2026-08-17-exp13-geneeffect-residual-protocol.md"] -->|Guides Feature Blocks| ModelFeats["src/model/geneeffect.py"]
  ResultDir["docs/results/joint_geneeffect_seed0/"] -->|Records Checkpoint Artifact| BestPt["outputs/joint_seed0_20260906T174818Z_b1024/best.pt"]
```

Sources: `docs/01-blueprint.md:1-126`, `docs/03-geneeffect-protocol.md:1-130`, `docs/specs/2026-08-17-exp13-geneeffect-residual-protocol.md:1-102`, `docs/results/p1_response_pathway_diagnostics/README.md:1-15`

---

## 2. The Freeze Rule and Vault Discipline

The primary operational rule governing the vault is the **Freeze Rule**: `docs/01-blueprint.md` is frozen. Edits must occur in place via dated paragraphs or restatements—never by appending unauthorized "v2" or revision files that contradict the core contract [.claude/skills/research-vault/SKILL.md:31-37]().

The vault functions as an instantaneous snapshot of current scientific state rather than an append-only changelog. Superseded designs retain a single `**Status:** retired` line and a link to their final result archive [.claude/skills/research-vault/SKILL.md:38-43]().

Sources: `.claude/skills/research-vault/SKILL.md:31-43`

---

## 3. Agent Instruction Files and Multi-Agent Configuration

The repository implements a structured agent instruction ecosystem under `.codex/` and `.claude/skills/` to regulate multi-agent workflows, model reasoning behaviors, and domain boundaries.

### Codex Multi-Agent Configuration

The project-local Codex configuration (`.codex/config.toml`) establishes approval policies, sandbox execution modes, and MCP server bindings (such as `context7` and `codebase-memory-mcp`) [.codex/config.toml:1-46](). It registers specialized subagents via `.codex/AGENTS.md` and dedicated TOML configuration files:

- **`domain_mapper`**: Read-only mapper for code, data, config, and documentation paths (`.codex/agents/domain-mapper.toml`) [.codex/config.toml:22-24](). It restricts modifications, requiring inspection of `src/data`, `src/model`, `src/training`, and `src/eval` [.codex/agents/domain-mapper.toml:7-13]().
- **`experiment_planner`**: Read-only planner for experiment configs and verification designs across the Exp13 GeneEffect residual benchmark [.codex/config.toml:26-29]().
- **`implementation_worker`**: Scoped code and config editing worker acting under explicit parent assignment [.codex/config.toml:30-32]().
- **`reviewer`**: Adversarial review agent focused on data leakage, silent defaults, data contracts, and missing tests [.codex/config.toml:34-36]().
- **`docs_guard`**: Read-only documentation guard protecting `docs/`, `README.md`, and agent instructions against drift [.codex/config.toml:38-41]().

### Diagram: Natural Language Space to Code Entity Space (Agent Infrastructure)

```mermaid
graph TD
  Skill["/.claude/skills/research-vault/SKILL.md"] -->|Enforces Authority Rule| VaultDocs["docs/01-blueprint.md"]
  CodexCfg[".codex/config.toml"] -->|Spawns Domain Mapper| MapperCfg[".codex/agents/domain-mapper.toml"]
  MapperCfg -->|Restricts Scope to Package| SrcPkg["src/data, src/model, src/training"]
  AgentsMd[".codex/AGENTS.md"] -->|Defines Reviewer Role| ReviewerCfg[".codex/agents/reviewer.toml"]
```

Sources: `.codex/config.toml:1-46`, `.codex/AGENTS.md:1-29`, `.codex/agents/domain-mapper.toml:1-13`, `.claude/skills/research-vault/SKILL.md:1-50`

---

## 4. Result Registration and Status Synchronization

To maintain evidentiary integrity, planned numbers or expected metrics are strictly prohibited from entering the vault. Results enter the documentation vault only after analysis execution is complete and verified against leak-detection gates [.claude/skills/research-vault/SKILL.md:50-59]().

### Result Registration Lifecycle

1. **Execution**: Run analyses and preserve required outputs (config, seeds, commit SHA, per-fold outputs, and hashes) [.claude/skills/research-vault/SKILL.md:55-56]().
2. **Admissibility Check**: Audit leakage and integrity rules defined in `docs/01-blueprint.md` §7 and protocol leakage sections [.claude/skills/research-vault/SKILL.md:57-59]().
3. **Verdict Classification**: Record outcomes using standard vocabulary (`negative`, `paused`, `closed`, `scope-closed`, `reportable-but-not-claimable`) [.claude/skills/research-vault/SKILL.md:60-62]().
4. **Drafting Evidence**: Author `docs/results/<slug.md>` following standard sections: Status, What was tested, Method and provenance, Result, Interpretation, Verdict and scope, and Reproduction [.claude/skills/research-vault/SKILL.md:63-65]().
5. **Status Sync**: Manually reconcile status strings across the root `README.md`, `docs/01-blueprint.md`, and active protocols, as no automated script enforces cross-file state synchronization [.claude/skills/research-vault/SKILL.md:71-78]().

Sources: `.claude/skills/research-vault/SKILL.md:50-78`

---

- [docs/specs/2026-09-07-p1b_response_functionality_interface_adaptation_diagnostic.md](docs/specs/2026-09-07-p1b_response_functionality_interface_adaptation_diagnostic.md)

- [tests/test_benchmark_split.py](tests/test_benchmark_split.py)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

This page documents the formal scientific protocols, benchmark splits, and raw data ingestion references governing the gene-perturbation prediction pipeline. It covers the held-out cell-line GeneEffect residual protocol, the 226-cell-line validation/test split structure, eligibility enforcement guards, and foundational datasets including DepMap 26Q1 and Perturb-seq collections [docs/03-geneeffect-protocol.md:1-16](), [tests/test_benchmark_split.py:1-7]().

---

## 1. GeneEffect Residual Protocol

The core prediction track under the research blueprint evaluates whether a single-cell perturbation-response model learns cell-line context information that improves held-out line dependency prediction beyond simple gene means and context ridges [docs/03-geneeffect-protocol.md:17-37]().

For a held-out cell line $c$ and target gene $g$, the model predicts the DepMap GeneEffect $y_{g,c}$ as a residual over a fixed training gene mean [docs/03-geneeffect-protocol.md:17-26]():

$$\hat y_{g,c} = \mu_{\text{train}}(g) + \hat\delta(g,c), \qquad \mu_{\text{train}}(g) = \operatorname{mean}_{c\in\mathcal C_{\text{train}}} y_{g,c}$$

- **Generalization Axis**: Generalization is strictly across **cell lines**, not unseen genes [docs/03-geneeffect-protocol.md:29-32]().
- **Data Leakage Prevention**: No GeneEffect measurement of the held-out line $c$ enters the deployable feature path or normalization statistics [docs/03-geneeffect-protocol.md:29-32]().
- **Inputs**: Frozen Tx1-3B basal embeddings ($128$ sampled cells per line), ESM-2 protein embeddings ($e_g \in \mathbb{R}^{1280}$), precomputed basal gene statistics $q_{g,c}$, and response anchors [docs/03-geneeffect-protocol.md:59-90]().

Sources: `docs/03-geneeffect-protocol.md:1-37`

---

## 2. The 226-Cell-Line Split and Eligibility Guards

Membership authority for training, validation, and testing is fixed by `configs/benchmarks/cell_line_geneeffect_226_split.json` [docs/03-geneeffect-protocol.md:38-56](), [configs/benchmarks/cell_line_geneeffect_226_split.json:1-240]().

### Cohort Distribution

| Cohort | Total Members | Labeled Members | Role & Description |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | :--- |
| **train** | 172 | 170 | Supervised fitting; includes 47 original basal contexts and 125 patient-grouped atlas lines. `ACH-000779` (PC9) and `ACH-001086` (HeLa) are unlabeled train members [docs/03-geneeffect-protocol.md:44-50](), [tests/test_benchmark_split.py:104-108]() |
| **val** | 27 | 27 | Once-per-epoch evaluation, checkpoint selection, and early stopping [docs/03-geneeffect-protocol.md:47-47]() |
| **test** | 27 | 27 | One-shot final evaluation cohort, strictly isolated until model selection concludes [docs/03-geneeffect-protocol.md:48-48]() |

### Eligibility Enforcement Guard

Every fitting routine passes through strict eligibility validation implemented in `src/data/splits.py` (tested via `tests/test_benchmark_split.py`) [tests/test_benchmark_split.py:1-7](). The function `assert_fit_eligible` verifies that a given `model_id` belongs to the labeled training cohort, raising a `ValueError` if leakage or an unlabeled train member (such as PC9 or HeLa) is passed to a supervised fit [tests/test_benchmark_split.py:30-56]().

Sources: `docs/03-geneeffect-protocol.md:38-56`, `configs/benchmarks/cell_line_geneeffect_226_split.json:1-240`, `tests/test_benchmark_split.py:1-134`

---

## 3. Datasets: DepMap 26Q1 and Perturb-seq Collections

The pipeline integrates population-level CRISPR screening data with single-cell perturbation expression data.

### DepMap Public 26Q1
Used as the primary dependency label source for continuous CRISPR gene-effect scores ($\text{CRISPRGeneEffect.csv}$) and model metadata (`Model.csv`) [docs/data/depmap-public-26q1.md:1-17](). 
- **K562 Mapping**: Pinned to ModelID `ACH-000551` (`K-562`, CCLE name `K562_HAEMATOPOIETIC_AND_LYMPHOID_TISSUE`) [docs/data/depmap-public-26q1.md:38-45]().
- **Semantics**: Gene-effect scores represent population-level cell fitness changes under targeted CRISPR knockout, not single-cell death events [docs/data/depmap-public-26q1.md:5-7]().

### Perturb-seq Datasets
- **Dixit K562 Perturb-seq**: Early transcription-factor CRISPR-KO single-cell response dataset (`dixit_2016.h5ad`, 99,722 cells $\times$ 18,531 genes) used for response-to-dependency alignment sanity checks [docs/data/dixit-k562-perturbseq.md:1-29]().
- **Response Anchors**: Four training cell lines (`ACH-000551` K562, `ACH-000971` HCT116, `ACH-000995` Jurkat, `ACH-000739` HepG2) provide genetic perturbation responses and non-targeting controls [docs/03-geneeffect-protocol.md:68-76]().

Sources: `docs/data/depmap-public-26q1.md:1-53`, `docs/data/dixit-k562-perturbseq.md:1-63`, `docs/03-geneeffect-protocol.md:68-76`

---

# Page: Data Preparation and Caches

# Data Preparation and Caches

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/data/prepared.py](src/data/prepared.py)
- [src/data/tx1_cache.py](src/data/tx1_cache.py)
- [src/experiments/prepare.py](src/experiments/prepare.py)
- [tests/test_joint_integration.py](tests/test_joint_integration.py)
- [tests/test_tx1_embed_cache.py](tests/test_tx1_embed_cache.py)

</details>



The data preparation phase provides an immutable, offline pipeline [src/experiments/prepare.py:1-95]() that transforms raw single-cell UMI counts, perturbation matrices, and protein metadata into deterministic, standardized caches and configuration manifests (`prepared_inputs.json`). By decoupling resource-intensive ingestion—such as executing the Tx1-3B single-cell encoder [src/data/tx1_cache.py:1-48]() or parsing massive H5AD/parquet archives—from the active training loop, the system guarantees reproducible training runs and low I/O latency across distributed workers.

```mermaid
graph TD
    sub5["Raw Inputs"] -->| "src/experiments/prepare.py" | prep["prepare_inputs"]
    prep -->| "src/data/tx1_cache.py" | tx1["Tx1BasalCache"]
    prep -->| "src/data/response_cache.py" | resp["ResponseTargetsCache"]
    prep -->| "src/data/embeddings.py" | esm["ESM2Embeddings"]
    prep -->| "src/data/q_sc.py" | qsc["QScFeatures"]
    tx1 -->| "PreparedInputs" | trainer["src/training/"]
    resp -->| "PreparedInputs" | trainer
    esm -->| "PreparedInputs" | trainer
    qsc -->| "PreparedInputs" | trainer
```
*Sources: [src/experiments/prepare.py:94-172](), [src/data/tx1_cache.py:1-48](), [src/data/prepared.py:30-66]()*

---

## 2.1 Tx1 Basal Embedding Cache

The Tx1 basal embedding subsystem manages encoder-agnostic cell line embeddings [src/data/tx1_cache.py:1-48](). It uses an injected `EncoderFn` callable to process raw control cells, writing per-cell `tahoe_x1_3b` vector arrays alongside provenance sidecars [src/data/tx1_cache.py:59-73]() and HVG gene-order constraints [src/data/tx1_cache.py:31-38](). The verification pipeline (`verify_cache`) enforces strict schema versions, exact embedding widths (`EMBEDDING_WIDTH = 2560`) [src/data/tx1_cache.py:46](), and cryptographic authentication against pinned Phase-A registration manifests [src/data/tx1_cache.py:136-164]().

For detailed implementation, atomicity guarantees, and sharding strategies, see [Tx1 Basal Embedding Cache](#2.1).

```mermaid
graph TD
    raw["RawAnnData"] -->| "embed_lines" | enc["EncoderFn"]
    enc -->| "write_line_cache" | cache["LineCacheDirectory"]
    cache -->| "verify_cache" | val["ValidationAndProvenance"]
```
*Sources: [src/data/tx1_cache.py:1-48](), [src/data/tx1_cache.py:136-164]()*

---

## 2.2 Response Caches and Streaming

During response prediction training, the pipeline loads sparse perturbations and sampled cell-state distributions using memory-mapped structures [src/data/response_cache.py:1-30](). Response gene bags curate target distributions across training anchors, aligning single-cell response counts with high-variable gene panels [src/data/response.py:1-50](). Streaming loaders fetch these records dynamically to minimize memory overhead during batch construction [src/data/prepared.py:30-66]().

For detailed mechanics on gene bags, memory-mapped caching, and streaming loaders, see [Response Caches and Streaming](#2.2).

```mermaid
graph TD
    bags["assemble_train_response_gene_bags"] -->| "write_response_targets_cache" | rc["ResponseTargetsCache"]
    rc -->| "open_response_targets_cache" | stream["StreamingLoader"]
```
*Sources: [src/experiments/prepare.py:141-151](), [src/data/prepared.py:21-25]()*

---

## 2.3 Gene and Protein Feature Tables

Model conditioning relies on static feature tables precomputed prior to training [src/experiments/prepare.py:94-172](). This includes ESM2 protein language model embedding unions [src/data/embeddings.py:1-40](), UniProt offline cache bootstraps, single-cell quality control metrics (`q_sc` caches) [src/data/q_sc.py:1-35](), and copy-number variation priors derived from reference donors like K562 (`ACH-000551`) [src/experiments/prepare.py:125-133](). These tables align gene symbols across disparate DepMap and Perturb-seq datasets into unified evaluation splits [src/data/geneeffect.py:1-60]().

For deeper coverage of ESM2 precomputations, copy priors, and split configurations, see [Gene and Protein Feature Tables](#2.3).

```mermaid
graph TD
    labels["load_geneeffect_long"] -->| "build_coverage_universe" | univ["CoverageUniverse"]
    univ -->| "write_embedding_union" | esm["ESM2UnionTable"]
    univ -->| "build_q_sc_shards" | qsc["QScCache"]
```
*Sources: [src/experiments/prepare.py:124-134](), [src/data/q_sc.py:1-35]() *

---

## 2.4 Raw Data Ingestion Scripts

Raw inputs are gathered and normalized via dedicated builder scripts located under `src/data/prepare/` and executed through orchestration entrypoints [src/experiments/prepare.py:1-95](). These builders ingest raw UMI matrices from Tahoe downloads, Kinker cancer dependency files, and atlas sources, registering them into centralized source registries [src/data/geneeffect.py:1-60](). Scripts validate dataset integrity and guarantee input immutability before downstream training phases begin [src/experiments/prepare.py:118-120]().

For details on source registries, Tahoe downloads, and builder execution scripts, see [Raw Data Ingestion Scripts](#2.4).

```mermaid

    cli["hpc/run.sh prepare"] -->| "parse_config" | prep["prepare_inputs"]

    reg -->| "materialize" | raw["RawUMI_AnnData"]
```
*Sources: [src/experiments/prepare.py:94-135](), [src/data/geneeffect.py:1-60]()*

## 2.5 Datasets, Batching and Sampling

The prepared dataset layer bridges immutable on-disk caches to PyTorch data loaders [src/data/prepared.py:1-66](). Modules such as `src/data/datasets.py` and `src/training/sampling.py` ingest the JSON manifest (`prepared_inputs.json`) [src/data/prepared.py:26-28]() to construct context batches, sample paired control-perturbation vectors, and manage memory-mapped pointers during training loops.

# Page: Tx1 Basal Embedding Cache

# Tx1 Basal Embedding Cache

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/data/tx1_cache.py](src/data/tx1_cache.py)
- [src/experiments/prepare.py](src/experiments/prepare.py)
- [tests/test_joint_integration.py](tests/test_joint_integration.py)
- [tests/test_tx1_basal.py](tests/test_tx1_basal.py)
- [tests/test_tx1_embed_cache.py](tests/test_tx1_embed_cache.py)
- [tests/test_tx1_response_data.py](tests/test_tx1_response_data.py)

</details>



The Tx1 Basal Embedding Cache system (`src/data/tx1_cache.py`) provides an encoder-agnostic storage, retrieval, and verification layer for Tx1-3B basal cell embeddings (`tahoe_x1_3b`, `EMBEDDING_WIDTH = 2560`) and Highly Variable Gene (HVG) expressions [src/data/tx1_cache.py:1-46](). It ensures immutability, atomic writes via staging directories, strict provenance tracking through metadata sidecars, and automated verification (`verify_cache`) prior to downstream model ingestion [src/data/tx1_cache.py:1-75]().

Sources: [src/data/tx1_cache.py:1-75](), [src/experiments/prepare.py:42-91]()

---

## Directory Layout and Sharding Architecture

Each cell line (`model_id`) in the dataset maintains an isolated subdirectory under the primary cache root. Within each line directory, arrays and sidecars are stored using strict naming conventions and binary formats (`.npy`, `.parquet`, `.json`).

```
cache_root/
├── ACH-000001/
│   ├── embeddings.npy          # Float32 array of shape (n_cells, 2560)
│   ├── hvg.npy                 # Float32 array of shape (n_cells, n_hvg_genes)
│   ├── obs.parquet             # Cell metadata DataFrame (obs)
│   ├── run_manifest.json       # Array shapes and schema version
│   ├── hvg_gene_order.json     # HVG gene order hash sidecar
│   ├── sample_provenance.json  # Cell selection, seed, and cap metadata
│   └── encoder_settings.json   # Tx1 model parameters and batch configs
├── ACH-000002/
...
```

### Core File Artifacts Table

| Artifact Name | File Format | Shape / Schema | Role |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `embeddings.npy` | NumPy binary | `(n_cells, 2560)` | Cached Tx1-3B basal cell representations [src/data/tx1_cache.py:46]() |
| `hvg.npy` | NumPy binary | `(n_cells, n_genes)` | Aligned log-normalized counts for HVG panel |
| `obs.parquet` | Apache Parquet | `DataFrame` | Cell indices, barcodes, and experimental identifiers |
| `run_manifest.json` | JSON | Object | Records array dimensions, `_SCHEMA_VERSION`, and checksums |
| `hvg_gene_order.json` | JSON | Object | Tracks the STATE model's expected gene order hash [src/data/tx1_cache.py:59-65]() |
| `sample_provenance.json`| JSON | Object | Records sampling seed, cell cap, and extracted cell barcodes [src/data/tx1_cache.py:67-71]() |

Sources: [src/data/tx1_cache.py:44-75](), [src/experiments/prepare.py:42-90]()

---

## Key Functions and Implementation Details

### Writing Caches Atomically (`write_line_cache`)
To prevent partial writes or corrupted files during concurrent execution or interruption, `write_line_cache` writes all artifacts into a temporary sibling directory (using a UUID suffix) before performing an atomic directory rename (`os.replace`) into the final `cache_dir / model_id` location.

```python
# Conceptual flow inside write_line_cache
tmp_dir = cache_dir / f".tmp_{model_id}_{uuid.uuid4().hex}"
tmp_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
# Serialize embeddings.npy, hvg.npy, obs.parquet, run_manifest.json
os.replace(tmp_dir, cache_dir / model_id)
```

### Verification and Integrity (`verify_cache` / `_verify_line`)
The `verify_cache` function inspects the entire cache tree to validate:
1. Presence of required files (`embeddings.npy`, `hvg.npy`, `obs.parquet`, `run_manifest.json`).
2. Shape consistency between metadata declarations and NumPy array dimensions.
3. Unit-norm properties of the embedding space (`_UNIT_NORM_ATOL`).
4. HVG gene order consistency via `hvg_gene_order.json`.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "VerificationPipeline"
        L["verify_cache\n(src/data/tx1_cache.py)"] --> M["_verify_line\n(src/data/tx1_cache.py)"]
        M --> N["_load_line_cache_arrays\n(src/data/tx1_cache.py)"]
        N --> O["CheckDimensionsAndSchema\n(src/data/tx1_cache.py)"]
        O --> P["ValidateUnitNorm\n(src/data/tx1_cache.py)"]
    end

    style L fill:#none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:2px
    style M fill:#none,stroke:#none
    style N fill:#none,stroke:#none
    style O fill:#none,stroke:#none
    style P fill:#none,stroke:#none
```

Sources: [src/data/tx1_cache.py:100-350](), [tests/test_tx1_embed_cache.py:1-102]()

---

## Provenance Sidecars and Authority Controls

### Registration Authentication
Before embedding or loading cached assets, Stage 2 enforces rigid authority checks against pinned cryptographic digests. `authenticate_tx1_registration` verifies the SHA-256 hash of the Phase-A registration JSON against `PINNED_TX1_REGISTRATION_SHA256` [src/data/tx1_cache.py:52-54, 136-164]().

### Provenance Sidecars
- **`hvg_gene_order.json`**: Records the SHA-256 hash of the gene order list against which `hvg.npy` was projected, ensuring downstream models receive features aligned with the STATE backbone [src/data/tx1_cache.py:59-65]().
- **`sample_provenance.json`**: Captures deterministic sampling seeds, maximum cell caps per line, and exact cell indices selected during extraction [src/data/tx1_cache.py:67-71]().
- **`encoder_settings.json`**: Documents batch sizes, sequence length caps, and checkpoint directories used during inference [src/experiments/prepare.py:77-90]().

Sources: [src/data/tx1_cache.py:50-80](), [src/experiments/prepare.py:77-90](), [tests/test_tx1_embed_cache.py:86-102]()

# Page: Response Caches and Streaming

# Response Caches and Streaming

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/data/response_cache.py](src/data/response_cache.py)
- [src/data/response_streaming.py](src/data/response_streaming.py)
- [tests/test_tx1_predicted_response.py](tests/test_tx1_predicted_response.py)
- [tests/test_tx1_response_gene_bags_cache.py](tests/test_tx1_response_gene_bags_cache.py)
- [tests/test_tx1_response_streaming.py](tests/test_tx1_response_streaming.py)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope
This page details the implementation of response gene bags, memory-mapped response target caches, memory-bounded streaming loaders, and predicted-response cache controls within the codebase. These modules govern how observed cellular response states and baseline controls are ingested, stored on disk via memory-mapped layouts, streamed under tight memory budgets, and validated against canonical HVG orders.

Sources: `src/data/response_cache.py:1-46`, `src/data/response_streaming.py:1-43`

---

## 1. Memory-Mapped Response Targets (`ResponseTargetsCache`)

Observed response targets are stored using structured memory-mapped files to allow random access to multi-cell gene bags without holding entire datasets in RAM. The core data structure is `ResponseTargetsCache`, defined in `src/data/response_cache.py:27-36`.

### On-Disk Layout and Schema
The response cache directory contains a manifest file (`manifest.json`), a metadata table (`metadata.parquet`), and three binary array files (`target_cells.npy`, `offsets.npy`, `genes.npy`) adhering to schema version `1` (`src/data/response_cache.py:17-25`).

- `target_cells.npy`: A 2D `float32` array containing concatenated expression vectors for all cells across all bags, shaped `[total_cells, len(hvg_order)]` (`src/data/response_cache.py:126-135`).
- `offsets.npy`: An `int64` array of shape `[n_bags + 1]` marking the start and stop indices in `target_cells.npy` for each response bag (`src/data/response_cache.py:136-151`).
- `metadata.parquet`: A table tracking bag provenance containing columns `perturbation_gene`, `model_id`, and `n_cells` (`src/data/response_cache.py:152-159`).

### Key Functions
- `normalize_response_metadata`: Canonicalizes perturbation symbols by stripping whitespace, converting to uppercase, and checking for duplicate normalized conditions (`src/data/response_cache.py:47-58`).
- `open_response_targets_cache`: Validates manifest schema versions, HVG matching, array data types, offset monotonicity, and returns a initialized `ResponseTargetsCache` instance (`src/data/response_cache.py:61-174`).
- `ResponseTargetsCache.target_bag`: Slices the memory-mapped `target_cells` array using `offsets` to return the cell expression matrix for a specific bag index (`src/data/response_cache.py:41-45`).

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["manifest.json"] --> B["open_response_targets_cache"]
    C["metadata.parquet"] --> B
    D["offsets.npy"] --> B
    E["target_cells.npy"] --> B
    B --> F["ResponseTargetsCache"]
    F --> G["target_bag(index: int)"]
```
Sources: `src/data/response_cache.py:17-174`, `tests/test_tx1_response_gene_bags_cache.py:32-62`

---

## 2. Streaming Loaders and Reservoir Draining

To prevent out-of-memory errors when processing massive datasets (such as HCT116 with over 18,000 perturbed genes where unflattened Python lists consume hundreds of gigabytes), the system uses a memory-bounded streaming and reservoir-draining pipeline (`src/data/response_streaming.py:1-43`).

### Reservoir Draining Algorithm
`drain_gene_reservoirs_to_matrix` builds a compressed sparse row (`csr_matrix`) from per-gene cell reservoirs while actively mutating and draining the reservoir in place (`src/data/response_streaming.py:86-122`).

1. **Total Budget Resolution**: `resolve_total_budget_keep_mask` computes an optional deterministic boolean mask across cells if a total cell budget is specified (`src/data/response_streaming.py:57-84`).
2. **In-Place Draining**: As cells are consumed from reservoirs sorted by gene name, processed slots are explicitly set to `None`. This allows Python's garbage collector to reclaim memory immediately rather than retaining references until the entire builder returns (`src/data/response_streaming.py:32-37`).
3. **Vectorized CSR Construction**: Component arrays (`indices`, `indptr`, `data`) are assembled using vectorized numpy routines rather than plain Python boxed-list iterations (`src/data/response_streaming.py:26-37`).

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["reservoirs: Mapping[str, MutableSequence]"] --> B["drain_gene_reservoirs_to_matrix"]
    C["metadata: pd.DataFrame"] --> B
    B --> D["resolve_total_budget_keep_mask"]
    D --> E["In-place slot nulling"]
    E --> F["csr_matrix"]
```
Sources: `src/data/response_streaming.py:1-146`, `tests/test_tx1_response_streaming.py:68-158`

---

## 3. Predicted-Response Caches and Control Cell Chunking

When evaluating predicted response states or establishing baseline controls, cell indices must be grouped into deterministic batches or windows.

### Control Cell Chunking
The helper `_chunk_control_cell_indices` divides control cell pools into fixed-size sets, handling tail padding deterministically using a configurable random seed (`tests/test_tx1_response_gene_bags_cache.py:148-164`). Because tail window filling depends on the seed, the seed forms part of cache fingerprints.

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["ControlCellPool"] --> B["_chunk_control_cell_indices"]
    B --> C["Seed-sensitive padding"]
    C --> D["Chunked Control Batches"]
```
Sources: `tests/test_tx1_predicted_response.py:13-164`, `tests/test_tx1_response_gene_bags_cache.py:148-164`

---

## Purpose and Scope

This page documents the immutable input-preparation phase and its underlying feature tables, offline caches, data structures, and membership splits. The system relies on strictly verified precomputed caches for protein language model embeddings (ESM2), UniProt offline provenance records, single-cell count population summaries (`q_sc`), the K562 copy prior, and fixed 226-cell-line train/val/test partitions. These structures isolate the training loop from raw single-cell AnnData files and remote web services during execution.

---

## 1. Cell Line Splits and Authority

Line partitioning is governed by fixed JSON configuration files that establish strict membership for the 226 DepMap cell lines. The codebase implements split management via `FixedSplit` and `Exp13Split` dataclasses, which enforce disjoint train, validation, and test partitions, as well as designated unlabeled training lines.

```mermaid
graph TD
    SplitJSON["FixedSplit JSON Config"] --> LoadSplit["load_geneeffect_226_split()"]
    LoadSplit --> Validate["validate_fixed_split()"]
    Validate --> FS["FixedSplit Object"]
    FS --> Train["train tuple (172 lines)"]
    FS --> Val["val tuple (27 lines)"]
    FS --> Test["test tuple (27 lines)"]
    FS --> Unlabeled["unlabeled_train tuple (ACH-000779, ACH-001086)"]
    
    style SplitJSON fill:none,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
    style LoadSplit fill:none,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
    style Validate fill:none,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
    style FS fill:none,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
```

*Figure 1: Split Validation and Authority Dataflow.*

* `FixedSplit` defines line partitions where models and context metrics are fitted strictly on the training partition (`src/data/splits.py:10-34`()).
* `load_geneeffect_226_split` parses split JSON definitions, validating string types, duplicate entries, and partition disjointness (`src/data/splits.py:71-107`()).
* `assert_fit_eligible` acts as a hard guard, raising an error if an inference-only validation/test line or an unlabeled training line enters a fitting or training loop (`src/data/splits.py:110-140`()).
* `Exp13Split` provides strict validation against a pinned SHA-256 hash representing the canonical benchmark state (`src/data/geneeffect.py:51-76`(), `src/data/geneeffect.py:149-186`()).

Sources: `src/data/splits.py:1-140`(), `src/data/geneeffect.py:51-186`()

---

## 2. UniProt Offline Cache Bootstrap

To avoid runtime network dependencies on the UniProt API during ESM2 embedding precomputation, the pipeline bootstraps an offline cache of protein sequences, accessions, and gene identifiers governed by explicit source manifests.

```mermaid
graph TD
    Manifest["sources.json Manifest"] --> BC["build_cache()"]
    UnionCSV["union.csv Genes"] --> BC
    SeqTSV["sequences.tsv Sequences"] --> BC
    IdTSV["identities.tsv Accessions"] --> BC
    Legacy["legacy.json Cache"] --> BC
    Aliases["aliases.json Overrides"] --> BC
    BC --> OutputCache["cache.json Offline Cache"]

    style Manifest fill:none,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
    style BC fill:none,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
    style OutputCache fill:none,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
```

*Figure 2: UniProt Offline Cache Bootstrap Pipeline.*

* `build_cache` resolves primary protein sequences, UniProt accessions, and explicit alias overrides using a verified multi-artifact source bundle (`tests/test_bootstrap_exp13_uniprot_cache.py:40-88`()).
* Source manifests (`configs/benchmarks/exp13_uniprot_offline_sources.json`) pin the cryptographic SHA-256 hashes of all input files (`configs/benchmarks/exp13_uniprot_offline_sources.json:1-25`()).
* Accession aliases (`configs/benchmarks/exp13_uniprot_accession_aliases.json`) handle ambiguous gene symbols or multi-mapping entries like `GPR89A` and `H3C4` (`configs/benchmarks/exp13_uniprot_accession_aliases.json:1-22`()).
* Integrity checks reject any record where a sequence SHA-256 hash diverges from the pinned source manifest or legacy cache expectations (`tests/test_bootstrap_exp13_uniprot_cache.py:99-139`()).

Sources: `tests/test_bootstrap_exp13_uniprot_cache.py:1-185`(), `configs/benchmarks/exp13_uniprot_offline_sources.json:1-25`(), `configs/benchmarks/exp13_uniprot_accession_aliases.json:1-22`()

---

## 3. ESM2 Embedding Precomputation and Universe Construction

Protein language model features are precomputed for a union of scored genes and response-bag genes. The universe builder reconciles raw gene coverage requirements across splits before embedding table extraction.

```mermaid
graph TD
    Labels["DepMap GeneEffect Long Table"] --> Universe["build_coverage_universe()"]
    Split["Exp13Split Definition"] --> Universe
    Universe --> Scored["Scored Universe (Passes train/val filters)"]
    Scored --> Union["build_embedding_union()"]
    Union --> NPZ["esm2.npz Embedding Table"]
    NPZ --> Require["require_npz_coverage()"]

    style Labels fill:none,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
    style Universe fill:none,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
    style Union fill:none,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
    style NPZ fill:none,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
```

*Figure 3: Coverage Universe and ESM2 Embedding Union Construction.*

* `build_coverage_universe` evaluates coverage requirements per gene, assigning explicit drop reasons (such as `train_finite_lt5` or `val_finite_lt3`) when observation counts fall below thresholds (`tests/test_build_exp13_esm2_universe.py:48-54`()).
* `build_embedding_union` combines scored genes and response-only evaluation genes into a sorted, duplicate-free universe (`tests/test_build_exp13_esm2_universe.py:62-66`()).
* `require_npz_coverage` validates that precomputed `.npz` files match the expected symbol order, dimension width, and resolution flags exactly, throwing errors on dimension mismatches or unexpected symbols (`tests/test_build_exp13_esm2_universe.py:79-114`()).
* Provenance utilities authenticate ESM2 embedding tables and ensure complete vector coverage prior to model initialization (`tests/test_precompute_esm2_embeddings.py:26-28`()).

Sources: `tests/test_build_exp13_esm2_embeddings.py:1-200`(), `tests/test_build_exp13_esm2_universe.py:1-165`()

---

## 4. Single-Cell Count Population Summaries (`q_sc` Cache)

Single-cell auxiliary features are precomputed per cell line into isolated shards (`.npz`) containing population summaries derived from raw UMI counts.

| Shard Array Key | Shape | Dtype | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `model_id` | `()` (scalar) | string / object | DepMap model identifier (e.g., `ACH-000551`) |
| `gene_symbols` | `(N,)` | string / object | Canonical uppercase gene symbol panel |
| `values` | `(N, 3)` | `np.float32` | Population metrics: `[mean, detected_fraction, variance]` |
| `available` | `(N,)` | `np.bool_` | Boolean flag indicating valid quantification |

*Table 1: Shard Layout and Array Schemas for Prepared `q_sc` Caches.*

* `load_q_sc_line` opens prepared `q_sc` shards without consulting raw AnnData source files, verifying shapes, dtypes, model ID alignment, and gene ordering (`src/data/q_sc.py:29-115`()).
* `compute_q_sc` computes mean expression, detected fraction, and population variance directly from raw UMI count matrices (`src/data/q_sc.py:118-170`()). It enforces strict validation rules, requiring finite, non-negative, integer raw counts and rejecting non-raw representations (e.g., `log1p` transformed matrices) (`tests/test_build_exp13_q_sc_cache.py:15-60`()).

Sources: `src/data/q_sc.py:1-170`(), `tests/test_build_exp13_q_sc_cache.py:1-79`()

---

## 5. Copy Prior Materialization

The pipeline incorporates a K562-based copy-number/gene-effect prior (`copy_prior.csv`) derived from DepMap CRISPR gene effect tables.

* `materialize_copy_prior` extracts K562 gene effect data (using donor model ID `ACH-000551`), filters out missing values, and writes out the prior alongside a cryptographic manifest (`tests/test_build_exp13_copy_prior.py:36-47`()).
* Manifest validation guards against unpinned source modifications by verifying SHA-256 sums of incoming `CRISPRGeneEffect.csv` tables and output prior files (`tests/test_build_exp13_copy_prior.py:104-124`()).
* `restrict_scored_universe_to_copy_prior` applies a strict universe gate, flagging genes missing from the copy prior with `copy_prior_missing` drop reasons (`tests/test_build_exp13_copy_prior.py:136-158`()).

Sources: `tests/test_build_exp13_copy_prior.py:1-170`()

---

## Purpose and Scope

This section documents the raw data ingestion pipeline located in `src/data/prepare/`, the operational utility scripts in `scripts/`, and the source registries governing immutable input preparation [scripts/README.md:1-14](). The ingestion scripts transform raw single-cell RNA-seq count matrices (such as Kinker cell line screens, Tahoe shards, and published Perturb-seq datasets) into immutable, Tx1-contract-verified `AnnData` (`.h5ad`) bundles and provenance-tracked benchmark registries.

## 2. Kinker Raw UMI and CPM Ingestion Builders

The Kinker pipeline separates raw integer UMI count ingestion from normalized CPM sensitivity matrices. The script `src/data/prepare/prepare_kinker_umi_h5ad.py` enforces strict integer validation and reconciliation against selected cell metadata [tests/test_prepare_kinker_umi_h5ad.py:1-25]().

### Key Functions and Guards
- `build(args)`: Main entry point for the Kinker raw UMI builder [tests/test_prepare_kinker_umi_h5ad.py:23]().
- Non-integer check: Refuses non-integer matrices to prevent normalized or scaled values from entering raw count pipelines [tests/test_prepare_kinker_umi_h5ad.py:126-131]().
- Cell-line reconciliation: Asserts that the matrix row `Cell_line` matches the expected manifest selection [tests/test_prepare_kinker_umi_h5ad.py:134-149]().

```python
# Conceptual usage of the Kinker raw UMI build entrypoint
uv run python -m src.data.prepare.prepare_kinker_umi_h5ad --help
```
[scripts/README.md:11-11]()

Sources: [scripts/README.md:11-11](), [tests/test_prepare_kinker_umi_h5ad.py:1-190]()

- Symbol mapping: `_map_symbols_to_ensembl` filters ambiguous gene symbols and resolves Ensembl identifiers [tests/test_materialize_exp13_original47_raw_umi.py:7-43]().

## 4. Basal Registries and Context Screen Benchmarks

Context-conditioned SL ranking and gene effect prediction rely on locked basal registries (`configs/benchmarks/context_screen_v2_basal_registry.json`) and explicit split configurations (`configs/benchmarks/context_screen_v2_split.json`) [configs/benchmarks/context_screen_v2_basal_registry.json:1-101](), [configs/benchmarks/context_screen_v2_split.json:1-123]().

### Basal Registry Schema Structure

| Field | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `context` | String | Canonical cell line name (e.g., `A549`, `K562`, `PC9`) |
| `model_id` | String | DepMap ModelID (e.g., `ACH-000681`) |
| `basal_source` | String | Origin description and assay type |
| `artifact_path` | String | Relative path to raw count or AnnData artifact |
| `artifact_sha256` | String | Cryptographic checksum of input artifact |
| `artifact_status` | String | Verification status (`source_registered`, `tx1_contract_verified`) |

Sources: [configs/benchmarks/context_screen_v2_basal_registry.json:1-101](), [configs/benchmarks/context_screen_v2_split.json:1-123]()

### PC9 and HeLa Basal Preparation

The module `src/data/prepare/build_pc9_hela_basal.py` handles specific data repairs required for older or formatted matrices [tests/test_build_pc9_hela_basal.py:12-12]().
- Excel symbol repairs: `_repair_hela_symbols` corrects date-mangled gene symbols (e.g., `1-Mar` to `MARC1`) position-aware [tests/test_build_pc9_hela_basal.py:15-30]().
- Quality Control gating: `_minimum_qc_mask` filters cells by gene detection thresholds and mitochondrial content [tests/test_build_pc9_hela_basal.py:32-42]().

Sources: [tests/test_build_pc9_hela_basal.py:1-87](), [configs/benchmarks/context_screen_v2_basal_registry.json:1-101]()

## Purpose and Scope
This section details the data ingestion, dataset definition, batch construction, and sampling infrastructure defined in `src/data/datasets.py` [src/data/datasets.py:1-254](), `src/data/batches.py` [src/data/batches.py:1-319](), and `src/training/sampling.py` [src/training/sampling.py:1-122](). These modules consume serialized metadata (`prepared_inputs.json`) and backing arrays to supply deterministic, distributed training and evaluation batches for joint GeneEffect and response-replay training.

---

## 1. Prepared Inputs and Metadata Loading (`prepared_inputs.json`)
The immutable foundation for all datasets is initialized via `load_inputs()` in `src/data/prepared.py` [src/data/prepared.py:1-507](), which parses the `prepared_inputs.json` manifest. The manifest enforces schema version `geneeffect-joint-prepared-v1` [src/data/prepared.py:27-27]() and defines global partitions, common gene panels, HVG orders, ESM2 vectors, and response anchor pools [src/data/prepared.py:159-174]().

Each cell line's basal representations are encapsulated by `PreparedLine` [src/data/prepared.py:31-37](), holding pooled Tx1 control embeddings (`controls_tx1`), highly variable gene basal values (`basal_hvg`), and single-cell q-score features (`QScFeatures`).

```mermaid
graph TD
    subcode["Code Entity Space"]
    json["prepared_inputs.json"] -->|parsed by| load_inputs["src.data.prepared.load_inputs"]
    load_inputs -->|instantiates| PreparedInputs["src.data.prepared.PreparedInputs"]
    PreparedInputs -->|maps ModelID to| PreparedLine["src.data.prepared.PreparedLine"]
    PreparedLine -->|contains| controls_tx1["controls_tx1 : np.ndarray"]
    PreparedLine -->|contains| basal_hvg["basal_hvg : np.ndarray"]
    PreparedLine -->|contains| q_sc["q_sc : QScFeatures"]

    style json fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style load_inputs fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style PreparedInputs fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style PreparedLine fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style controls_tx1 fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style basal_hvg fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style q_sc fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
```

Sources: `src/data/prepared.py:1-508]`, `tests/test_joint_data.py:1-178]()`

---

## 2. Dataset Classes and Collators

`src/data/datasets.py` provides two primary PyTorch `Dataset` implementations for joint training and evaluation: `DependencyDataset` and `ResponseDataset`.

### `DependencyDataset`
`DependencyDataset` manages finite GeneEffect rows for train, validation, or test splits [src/data/datasets.py:30-84](). 
- **Initialization**: Filters `labels` by ModelIDs corresponding to the requested split (`supervised_train`, `val`, or `test`) [src/data/datasets.py:36-44](). Caches worker-device tensors for basal controls and HVG profiles [src/data/datasets.py:70-77]().
- **Context Pooling**: Computes pooled cell contexts (`z_c`) via `_pooled_context()` [src/data/datasets.py:23-28](), concatenating the mean and variance across Tx1 control embedding dimensions.
- **Collator (`collate`)**: Groups integer indices into a `DependencyBatch` [src/data/datasets.py:85-144]() containing an `OnlineConditionBatch`, residual target tensor, gene means, and a validity mask.

### `ResponseDataset`
`ResponseDataset` indexes prepared response conditions from the response targets cache, partitioned by holdout status (`holdout=True` or `False`) [src/data/datasets.py:147-167]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    subcode["Code Entity Space"]
    PreparedInputs["src.data.prepared.PreparedInputs"] -->|supplies rows| DependencyDataset["src.data.datasets.DependencyDataset"]
    DependencyDataset -->|calls _pooled_context| z_c["z_c : torch.Tensor"]
    DependencyDataset -->|executes collate| DependencyBatch["src.data.batches.DependencyBatch"]
    DependencyBatch -->|wraps| OnlineConditionBatch["src.data.batches.OnlineConditionBatch"]
    PreparedInputs -->|supplies response targets| ResponseDataset["src.data.datasets.ResponseDataset"]

    style PreparedInputs fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style DependencyDataset fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style z_c fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style DependencyBatch fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style OnlineConditionBatch fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style ResponseDataset fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
```

Sources: `src/data/datasets.py:1-255]()`

---

## 3. Batch Data Structures

Batch containers are defined in `src/data/batches.py` as immutable dataclasses with rigorous validation methods (`validate()`) [src/data/batches.py:1-319]().

- `FeatureBatch` [src/data/batches.py:11-82](): Unstandardized live head features including projection deltas, single-cell features, ESM2 vectors, and context tensors.
- `OnlineConditionBatch` [src/data/batches.py:84-175](): Differentiable joint response-feature inputs containing tuple sequences of control cell bags (`controls_tx1`, `basal_hvg`), target genes, model IDs, and alignment masks.
- `DependencyBatch`: Combines an `OnlineConditionBatch` with target residuals, training gene means, and row validity flags [src/data/datasets.py:133-141]().

Sources: `src/data/batches.py:1-320]`, `src/data/datasets.py:85-144]()`

---

## 4. Sampling and Loader Construction

Deterministic dependency epochs and independently cycling anchor replay are implemented in `src/training/sampling.py` [src/training/sampling.py:1-122]().

### `make_training_loaders`
`make_training_loaders()` builds a sharded PyTorch `DataLoader` for dependency training and an infinite iterator for response replay [src/training/sampling.py:52-120]().
- **Dependency Stream**: Uses PyTorch's `DistributedSampler` with `seed=0`, shuffling per epoch (`sampler.set_epoch(epoch)`) and dropping incomplete trailing batches (`drop_last=True`) [src/training/sampling.py:95-103]().
- **Response Replay Stream (`_balanced_replay`)**: Independent of DistributedSampler state, `_balanced_replay()` divides `response_batch_size` across exactly four response anchors (`response_anchors`) [src/training/sampling.py:17-50](). It cycles through condition indices using isolated random number generators initialized with `SeedSequence([0, epoch, rank, anchor])` [src/training/sampling.py:32-35]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    subcode["Code Entity Space"]
    make_training_loaders["src.training.sampling.make_training_loaders"] -->|instantiates| DistributedSampler["torch.utils.data.DistributedSampler"]
    DistributedSampler -->|feeds| DependencyLoader["DataLoader[DependencyBatch]"]
    make_training_loaders -->|instantiates| _balanced_replay["src.training.sampling._balanced_replay"]
    _balanced_replay -->|yields| ResponseBatch["ResponseBatch"]

    style make_training_loaders fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style DistributedSampler fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style DependencyLoader fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style _balanced_replay fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style ResponseBatch fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
```

Sources: `src/training/sampling.py:1-123]()`

---

## 5. Verification and Integration Tests

Data loading, batch validation, and sampling invariants are verified by the test suites in `tests/test_joint_data.py` [src/tests/test_joint_data.py:1-434]() and `tests/test_joint_sampling.py` [src/tests/test_joint_sampling.py:1-142](). Key tests ensure:
- Zero-drift reproducibility across epoch/rank restarts without global RNG pollution [tests/test_joint_sampling.py:45-65]().
- Strict exclusion of holdout response conditions from the training replay stream [tests/test_joint_sampling.py:21-44]().
- Validation failures on invalid response batch sizes (e.g. not divisible by four) or non-zero base runtime seeds [tests/test_joint_sampling.py:67-83]().

Sources: `tests/test_joint_data.py:1-434]`, `tests/test_joint_sampling.py:1-142]()`

# Page: Model Architecture

# Model Architecture

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:
