- [docs/specs/2026-07-23-tx1-st-geneeffect-backbone-design.md](docs/specs/2026-07-23-tx1-st-geneeffect-backbone-design.md)
- [src/model/features.py](src/model/features.py)
- [src/model/geneeffect.py](src/model/geneeffect.py)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

The model architecture module defines the end-to-end neural network pipeline used to predict cellular dependencies and gene perturbation responses. At its core, the system composes a state-transition dynamics backbone with a five-block residual head to map basal single-cell transcriptomes and target gene perturbations into DepMap GeneEffect scores and distributional response predictions [`src/model/geneeffect.py:22-24()`]. This page provides a high-level overview of the backbone adapters, feature extraction pipelines, residual heads, and loss formulations. For deep technical implementation details, refer to the respective child pages.

Sources: `src/model/geneeffect.py:22-24()`

---

## 3.1 STATE Backbone Adapters

The STATE backbone adapters encapsulate single-cell perturbation forward passes, handling context-conditioned bag predictions, chunking strategies for large cell populations, and distributed data-parallel (DDP) safety. The central orchestrator is the `GeneEffectE2EModel` class, which invokes the state transition models via `predict_bags` to simulate post-perturbation cellular states [`src/model/geneeffect.py:68-73()`].

For detailed implementation of `StateForwardAdapter`, `ForwardOnlyStateModel`, chunking mechanisms, DDP safety guards, and mock models, see [STATE Backbone Adapters](#3.1).

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph CodeEntitySpace["Code Entity Space"]
        GEE[GeneEffectE2EModel] -->|calls| PB[predict_bags]
        PB -->|invokes| ST[backbone: nn.Module]
        ST -->|processes| CT[controls_tx1]
    end
```
Sources: `src/model/geneeffect.py:68-73()`

---

## 3.2 GeneEffect Head and Features

The gene effect head subsystem extracts structured numerical descriptors from predicted cell bags and projects them through a five-block residual architecture (`GeneEffectResidualHead`). Features include sparse Johnson-Lindenstrauss projections (`FixedSparseProjection`), HVG panel metrics, and baseline representations [`src/model/features.py:71-116()`, `src/model/geneeffect.py:22-38()`]. Features are normalized using `BlockStandardizer` prior to head ingestion [`src/model/geneeffect.py:41-64()`].

For detailed information on the five-feature residual head, feature blocks, normalization routines, initialization, and loss functions, see [GeneEffect Head and Features](#3.2).

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph CodeEntitySpace["Code Entity Space"]
        FB[FeatureBatch] -->|standardizes| BS[BlockStandardizer]
        BS -->|transforms| SF[_standardize]
        SF -->|feeds| GERH[GeneEffectResidualHead]
        FSP[FixedSparseProjection] -->|projects| CP[delta_proj]
    end
```
Sources: `src/model/geneeffect.py:22-64()`, `src/model/features.py:71-116()`

---

## 3.3 Response Prediction and Distributional Losses

To evaluate the fidelity of predicted perturbation responses against empirical single-cell distributions, the architecture computes distributional metrics such as energy distance and mean-delta MSE [`src/model/features.py:10-11()`]. Bag padding, deterministic random number generator (RNG) isolation, and online feature computation ensure reproducible training dynamics across distributed nodes [`src/model/geneeffect.py:66-93()`].

For comprehensive coverage of bag padding strategies, energy distance calculations, mean-delta MSE formulations, and RNG isolation controls, see [Response Prediction and Distributional Losses](#3.3).

Sources: `src/model/geneeffect.py:66-93()`, `src/model/features.py:10-11()`

---

# Page: STATE Backbone Adapters

# STATE Backbone Adapters

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/experiments/profile_joint.py](src/experiments/profile_joint.py)
- [src/model/state.py](src/model/state.py)
- [tests/test_joint_objective.py](tests/test_joint_objective.py)
- [tests/test_state_core.py](tests/test_state_core.py)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope
This page documents the STATE backbone adapter subsystem (`src/model/state.py`), which acts as an integration layer between the modular perturbation head/joint trainer and the ArcInstitute STATE transition model backbone [src/model/state.py:34-40](). It covers `StateForwardAdapter`, support for mock architectures (`LinearMockStateModel`), batched condition chunking, memory-efficient tensor expansions, mixed-precision gradient preservation, and Distributed Data Parallel (DDP) safety considerations.

---

## 1. Core Classes and Mock Models

The backbone subsystem provides an abstraction boundary so that downstream modules interact uniformly with either real STATE checkpoints or lightweight test doubles.

### `LinearMockStateModel`
`LinearMockStateModel` is a lightweight, fully self-contained neural network that mimics the input-output shape signature of a STATE backbone [src/model/state.py:9-32](). It is used extensively in unit tests and local smoke runs where checkpoint assets are absent [tests/test_state_core.py:3-8]().

* **Inputs**: Expects a dictionary containing `ctrl_cell_emb` (basal cell embeddings) and `pert_emb` (perturbation embeddings) [src/model/state.py:25-30]().
* **Operation**: Concatenates basal and perturbation vectors along dimension 1 and passes them through a two-layer `nn.Sequential` block with a `GELU` activation [src/model/state.py:17-31]().

### `StateForwardAdapter`
`StateForwardAdapter` wraps an underlying STATE model (`state_model`), standardizing input formatting, batch annotations, and output extraction [src/model/state.py:34-40](). It handles three execution modes:
1. **Unpadded Single Condition (`forward`)**: Processes a single control cell tensor and perturbation vector for one gene [src/model/state.py:41-55]().
2. **Equal-Size Chunks (`forward_chunks`)**: Splits control matrices into equal-sized condition chunks [src/model/state.py:57-70]().
3. **Batched Condition Chunks (`forward_condition_chunks`)**: Packs multiple gene conditions into a single batched sequence pass to maximize GPU utilization [src/model/state.py:72-130]().

Diagram: STATE Backbone Integration Hierarchy

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["JointModel"] -->|"calls"| B["StateForwardAdapter"]
    B -->|"wraps"| C["state_model"]
    C -.->|"production"| D["ArcInstituteSTATE"]
    C -.->|"testing"| E["LinearMockStateModel"]
    
    classDef default stroke:#000,fill:none;
```
*Sources: `src/model/state.py:9-40](), [tests/test_state_core.py:32-44`*

---

## 2. Chunking and Batch Expansion

To handle varying batch layouts without kernel overheads, `StateForwardAdapter.forward_condition_chunks` implements batched condition expansion [src/model/state.py:72-130]().

### Validation and Constraints
Before executing a forward pass, the adapter verifies structural invariants:
* Perturbations must form a 2D tensor of shape `[chunks, features]` [src/model/state.py:80-81]().
* Control chunks, perturbation rows, gene names, and batch indices must align in length [src/model/state.py:82-89]().
* Chunk sizes must match the backbone's configured `cell_sentence_len` attribute [src/model/state.py:92-99]().

### Memory-Efficient Perturbation Expansion
Rather than invoking separate forward passes or independent reduction kernels per chunk, perturbations are expanded across the sentence length dimension in a single batched operation [src/model/state.py:106-112]():

```python
perturbation_cells = (
    perturbations.unsqueeze(1)
    .expand(-1, chunk_sizes[0], -1)
    .reshape(control_cells.shape[0], -1)
)
```[src/model/state.py:108-112]()

Diagram: StateForwardAdapter Chunking Flow

```mermaid
graph TD
    Z["BatchInputs"] --> A["StateForwardAdapter.forward_condition_chunks"]
    A --> B["ValidateChunkAlignment"]
    B --> C["ConcatControlChunks"]
    B --> D["ExpandPerturbations"]
    C & D --> E["_forward_state_prepared"]
    E --> F["StateModel.predict_step"]
    F --> G["CastToFP32"]
    G --> H["SplitOutputChunks"]
    
    classDef default stroke:#000,fill:none;
```
*Sources: `src/model/state.py:72-130](), [tests/test_state_core.py:48-85`*

---

## 3. Mixed-Precision and Gradient Preservation

STATE backbones often operate in lower-precision formats (`float16` or `bfloat16`) to conserve memory. `StateForwardAdapter` manages numerical stability and gradient flow across precision boundaries:

* **Single-Cast Normalization**: Output tensors from the backbone are converted to `float32` once prior to view splitting [src/model/state.py:125-129](). This avoids redundant casting operations and backward pass overheads for each condition chunk.
* **Gradient Equivalence**: Unit tests verify that running chunked, bfloat16-native forward passes yields identical gradient magnitudes and storage sharing behavior compared to unquantized reference computations [tests/test_state_core.py:115-138]().

---

## 4. DDP-Safety and Distributed Execution

When training joint models across multiple GPUs using HuggingFace `Accelerate`, backbone adapters must interoperate correctly with Distributed Data Parallel (DDP) wrappers.

* **Unused Parameter Handling**: Because certain perturbation embedding tables or conditioning projections may not receive gradients on every micro-step, launchers explicitly configure DDP to tolerate unused parameters [src/experiments/profile_joint.py:40-43]() via `DistributedDataParallelKwargs(find_unused_parameters=True)`.
* **Device Placement**: Probes and training routines validate that worker accelerators are active CUDA devices before invoking state forward passes [src/experiments/profile_joint.py:44-48]().

*Sources: `src/experiments/profile_joint.py:40-48](), [src/model/state.py:160-173`*

---

# Page: GeneEffect Head and Features

# GeneEffect Head and Features

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/model/features.py](src/model/features.py)
- [src/model/geneeffect.py](src/model/geneeffect.py)
- [src/model/initialization.py](src/model/initialization.py)
- [src/model/losses.py](src/model/losses.py)
- [src/model/normalization.py](src/model/normalization.py)
- [tests/test_geneeffect_e2e.py](tests/test_geneeffect_e2e.py)
- [tests/test_geneeffect_features.py](tests/test_geneeffect_features.py)
- [tests/test_geneeffect_head.py](tests/test_geneeffect_head.py)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope
This page details the implementation of the GeneEffect prediction head, the five input feature blocks (`delta_proj`, `s`, `q_sc`, `e_g`, `z_c`), the deterministic sparse Johnson-Lindenstrauss projection, the `BlockStandardizer` normalization layer, checkpoint initialization/warm-start protocols, and the Huber-based training loss.

Sources: [`src/model/geneeffect.py:22-142`]() [`src/model/features.py:42-138`]() [`src/model/normalization.py:25-169`]() [`src/model/initialization.py:52-124`]() [`src/model/losses.py:81-97`]()

---

## 1. Five-Feature Residual Head Architecture
The GeneEffect prediction system evaluates gene dependency scores by combining five distinct feature blocks through a residual MLP head, `GeneEffectResidualHead` [src/model/head.py:10](). The architecture is governed by `GeneEffectBlockConfig` [src/model/head.py:8](), which allows enabling or disabling individual feature blocks (e.g., for ablation studies).

The five feature blocks comprise:
1. `delta_proj`: Projected expression shift vector via `FixedSparseProjection` [src/model/features.py:71]().
2. `s`: Summary distribution statistics (energy distance, mean shift, own-gene shift, etc.) [src/model/features.py:47-54]().
3. `q_sc`: Single-cell query embeddings representing the cell line context.
4. `e_g`: ESM2 protein sequence embedding for the target gene [src/model/initialization.py:15]().
5. `z_c`: Basal state summary of the cell line context [src/model/losses.py:18-21]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    sub5[""OnlineConditionBatch"" --> src_model_geneeffect_GeneEffectE2EModel_condition_features]
    src_model_geneeffect_GeneEffectE2EModel_condition_features --> src_model_features_compute_condition_feature_batch
    src_model_features_compute_condition_feature_batch --> f_delta[""FeatureBatch.delta_proj""]
    src_model_features_compute_condition_feature_batch --> f_s[""FeatureBatch.s""]
    f_q[""FeatureBatch.q_sc""] --> norm[""BlockStandardizer.transform""]
    f_e[""FeatureBatch.e_g""] --> norm
    f_z[""FeatureBatch.z_c""] --> norm
    f_delta --> norm
    f_s --> norm
    norm --> head[""GeneEffectResidualHead""]
    head --> delta_hat[""delta_hat (GeneEffect Residual)""]
```
*Figure 1: Data flow from raw online condition batches through feature extraction, standardization, and the GeneEffect residual head.*

Sources: [`src/model/geneeffect.py:66-94`]() [`src/model/features.py:42-65`](), [`src/model/head.py:7-17`]()

---

## 2. Feature Engineering and Sparse Projection
Feature extraction turns predicted cell bags and basal references into fixed-width tensors suitable for the residual head.

### Sparse Johnson-Lindenstrauss Projection
`FixedSparseProjection` implements a deterministic, data-independent sparse JL projection using the Achlioptas distribution at density $\frac{1}{\sqrt{4000}}$ [src/model/features.py:71-88](). The projection matrix is generated once from a fixed seed (`PROJECTION_SEED = 0`), ensuring reproducible lower-dimensional embeddings of the high-dimensional expression shift space ($\Delta \in \mathbb{R}^{2 \times \text{HVG\_WIDTH}}$) [src/model/features.py:13-16, 71-88]().

```python
# Core sparse projection transformation pattern
projected = delta @ components.transpose(0, 1)
```
*Source code reference:* [`src/model/features.py:100-115`]()

### Vectorized Condition Features
`compute_condition_feature_batch` computes condition features over batch elements without incurring Python/CUDA round-trip overhead per row [src/model/features.py:158-167](). It evaluates summary metrics including energy distance, mean shifts, cosine similarities, and own-gene shift indicators [src/model/features.py:47-54, 100-115]().

Sources: [`src/model/features.py:42-191`]() [`tests/test_geneeffect_features.py:21-40`]()

---

## 3. Normalization via `BlockStandardizer`
Continuous feature blocks (`delta_proj`, `s`, `q_sc`, `e_g`, `z_c`) are standardized using `BlockStandardizer` before entering the residual head [src/model/normalization.py:15-26]().

### Fitting and Streaming
- **Batch Fitting (`fit`)**: Computes exact mean and scale across a pre-materialized training block mapping [src/model/normalization.py:40-75]().
- **Streamed Fitting (`fit_batches`)**: Computes population statistics incrementally using Welford's algorithm across data streams without loading all training rows into memory simultaneously [src/model/normalization.py:77-144]().
- **Constant Columns**: Features with zero standard deviation are automatically tracked and their scale factors are safely clamped to `1.0` to prevent division by zero [src/model/normalization.py:68-71]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    raw_blocks[""train_blocks / train_batches""] --> fit_method[""BlockStandardizer.fit / fit_batches""]
    fit_method --> stats[""_BlockStats (mean, scale, constant_columns)""]
    stats --> transform_method[""BlockStandardizer.transform""]
    transform_method --> standardized_tensor[""Normalized Feature Tensor""]
```
*Figure 2: Statistical fitting and transformation lifecycle inside `BlockStandardizer`.*

Sources: [`src/model/normalization.py:25-169`]()

---

## 4. Initialization and Warm-Start Protocols
Model construction and checkpoint restoration are managed in `src/model/initialization.py` [src/model/initialization.py:52-177]().

### Warm-Start State Dicts
`warm_start_state_dict` loads checkpoints manually via `torch.load` and filters keys by shape compatibility [src/model/initialization.py:52-105](). Any tensors with mismatched shapes are skipped while preserving freshly initialized parameters for new heads or dimensions, returning a `WarmStartReport` detailing loaded, skipped, missing, and unexpected keys [src/model/initialization.py:35-124]().

### Joint Model Assembly
`build_joint_model` constructs the complete `GeneEffectE2EModel` combining the STATE backbone, ESM2 adapters, projection matrices, and standardizers either from scratch or by restoring a fully self-contained checkpoint [src/model/initialization.py:134-177]().

Sources: [`src/model/initialization.py:34-177`]()

---

## 5. Objective Functions and Losses
Dependency prediction models are supervised using robust regression losses combined with permutation-invariant bag pooling [src/model/losses.py:11-97]().

### Moment Pooling
`moment_pool` summarizes per-cell bags into permutation-invariant representations [src/model/losses.py:11-46](). By default (`moments=2`), it computes concatenated mean and biased population variance across cell dimensions [src/model/losses.py:18-31]().

### GeneEffect Huber Loss
`geneeffect_loss` computes the mean FP32 Huber loss ($\delta=1.0$) exclusively over valid, labeled gene-context pairs, incorporating fail-closed checks for non-finite values or empty batches [src/model/losses.py:81-97]().

```python
def geneeffect_loss(
    prediction: torch.Tensor, target: torch.Tensor, valid: torch.Tensor
) -> torch.Tensor:
    return F.huber_loss(
        prediction.float()[valid], target.float()[valid], delta=1.0, reduction="mean"
    )
```
*Source code reference:* [`src/model/losses.py:81-97`]()

Sources: [`src/model/losses.py:11-97`]() [`tests/test_geneeffect_head.py:1-12`]()

---

# Page: Response Prediction and Distributional Losses

# Response Prediction and Distributional Losses

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/model/response.py](src/model/response.py)
- [tests/test_response_training.py](tests/test_response_training.py)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope
This page documents the technical design, implementation, and verification of response prediction and distributional loss formulations within the `src/model/response.py` and `tests/test_response_training.py` modules. The response prediction system evaluates gene perturbations at single-cell resolution by processing cell bags through the STATE backbone adapters, applying deterministic padding strategies to conform to fixed sentence-length constraints, and computing rigorous distributional metrics (`energy_distance` and `mean_delta_mse`) to capture both average shift and dispersion variations without mode collapse.

Sources:
- `src/model/response.py:1-250`
- `tests/test_response_training.py:1-177`

---

## 1. Response Prediction and Bag Padding (`predict_bags`)

When performing gene perturbation predictions across multi-cell conditions (bags), cell counts vary dynamically across cell lines and batches. However, the STATE backbone architecture enforces a strict fixed-window cell sentence length (`cell_sentence_len`) [src/model/response.py:18-24](). 

The `predict_bags` function coordinates ingestion of variable-length basal cell tensors, chunks them to match the required window sizes, handles deterministic padding via `_chunk_control_cell_indices`, forwards them through the network, and trims the outputs back to the original cell counts.

```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------+
|                        predict_bags()                           |
|  Inputs: controls (Sequence[Tensor]), genes (Sequence[str])     |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------+
                                 |
                                 v
+-----------------------------------------------------------------+
|               _state_window(model) Resolution                   |
|  Inspects model, DDP wrappers, and state_adapter for window     |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------+
                                 |
           +---------------------+---------------------+
           |                                           |
    (Window found)                              (No window / Test)
           |                                           |
           v                                           v
+-----------------------------+               +-------------------+
| _chunk_control_cell_indices |               | _seeded_model_    |
| - Deterministic NumPy RNG   |               |   forward()       |
| - Resampling w/ replacement |               +-------------------+
| - Chunks to cell_sentence_len|
+-----------------------------+
           |
           v
+-----------------------------------------------------------------+
|               _seeded_model_forward() execution                 |
|  - Training: standard rank RNG                                  |
|  - Evaluation: torch.random.fork_rng() isolated seed            |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------+
           |
           v
+-----------------------------------------------------------------+
|                     Trimming & Assembly                         |
|  Strips added padding rows; returns tuple of prediction tensors |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------+
```

Sources:
- `src/model/response.py:12-40`
- `src/model/response.py:78-96`
- `src/model/response.py:133-173`

---

## 2. Distributional Losses: Mean-Delta MSE and Energy Distance

To measure the accuracy of predicted cell response bags relative to observed experimental distributions, two primary loss formulations are utilized: `mean_delta_mse` and `energy_distance`.

### Mean-Delta MSE (`mean_delta_mse`)
Computes the mean squared error between the predicted and observed mean shifts relative to the control mean [src/model/response.py:43-55](). Explicitly retaining the control mean prevents the model from winning by simply reproducing absolute basal expression levels while ignoring the actual perturbation effect [src/model/response.py:48-52]().

$$\mathcal{L}_{\text{delta}} = \left\| \left(\frac{1}{N}\sum \hat{x} - \mu_{\text{ctrl}}\right) - \left(\frac{1}{M}\sum x - \mu_{\text{ctrl}}\right) \right\|_2^2$$

### Energy Distance (`energy_distance`)
Calculates the statistical energy distance between two empirical distributions (predicted cells $X$ and observed cells $Y$) [src/model/response.py:58-75]():

$$D_E(X, Y) = 2 \mathbb{E}\|X - Y\| - \mathbb{E}\|X - X'\| - \mathbb{E}\|Y - Y'\|$$

Unlike `mean_delta_mse`, energy distance is sensitive to changes in spread and dispersion [src/model/response.py:58-69](). This penalizes mode collapse—a failure mode where a model predicts the correct average perturbation shift while collapsing single-cell variance [src/model/response.py:62-66]().

Sources:
- `src/model/response.py:43-76`
- `tests/test_response_training.py:94-128`

---

## 3. RNG Isolation and Deterministic Evaluation

To guarantee reproducible evaluation metrics without polluting or mutating the global training random number generator state, `_seeded_model_forward` uses PyTorch's `fork_rng` context manager alongside explicit CUDA device seeding [src/model/response.py:114-131]().

```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------+
|                     _seeded_model_forward                       |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------+
                                 |
                        Is model.training?
                                 |
           +---------------------+---------------------+
           | Yes                                       | No
           v                                           v
+-----------------------------+               +-------------------+
| Execute normal model pass   |               | Resolve CUDA      |
| using rank-local RNG        |               | devices via       |
+-----------------------------+               | _cuda_rng_devices |
                                              +-------------------+
                                                       |
                                                       v
                                              +-------------------+
                                              | fork_rng(devices) |
                                              | - Set CPU seed    |
                                              | - Set CUDA manual |
                                              |   seeds per device|
                                              +-------------------+
                                                       |
                                                       v
                                              +-------------------+
                                              | Execute model     |
                                              | forward pass      |
                                              +-------------------+
```

Sources:
- `src/model/response.py:98-131`

---

# Joint Training System

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [tests/test_joint_distributed.py](tests/test_joint_distributed.py)
- [tests/test_joint_resume.py](tests/test_joint_resume.py)
- [tests/test_joint_training.py](tests/test_joint_training.py)

</details>



The Joint Training System unifies context-conditioned GeneEffect regression with recurring Perturb-seq response supervision into a single coherent training loop `[docs/specs/2026-09-06-modular-joint-training-design.md:10-21]`. By replacing historical staged training runs with a unified architecture, the system coordinates dependency batches and multi-anchor response replay updates simultaneously `[docs/specs/2026-09-06-modular-joint-training-design.md:80-94]`.

For details on child topics, refer to:
- [Trainer Loop and Objective](#4.1)
- [Configuration and CLI](#4.2)
- [Checkpointing, Resume and Distributed Execution](#4.3)
- [Performance Profiling and Throughput](#4.4)

```mermaid
graph TD
    sub5["NaturalLanguageSpace: Joint Training Pipeline"] -->|ImplementedBy| code5["CodeEntitySpace: Modules"]
    code5 --> T[src/training/trainer.py]
    code5 --> C[src/training/checkpoint.py]
    code5 --> D[src/training/distributed.py]
    code5 --> Config[src/experiments/config.py]
    
    T -->|"defines"| TU[train_update]
    T -->|"defines"| F[fit]
    C -->|"defines"| SC[save_checkpoint]
    D -->|"manages"| Acc[Accelerator]
```
Sources: `docs/specs/2026-09-06-modular-joint-training-design.md:10-21`, `src/training/trainer.py:31-176`

---

## 4.1 Trainer Loop and Objective

The training loop coordinates fine-grained gradient updates using Huber loss for GeneEffect prediction alongside mean-delta MSE and energy distance for response supervision `[docs/specs/2026-09-06-modular-joint-training-design.md:68-79]`. Every optimizer update processes a dependency batch, while periodic replay steps inject response supervision from four anchors (`K562`, `Jurkat`, `HepG2`, `HCT116`) at a configurable cadence (`src/training/trainer.py`) `[docs/specs/2026-09-06-modular-joint-training-design.md:80-94, src/training/trainer.py:53-118]`. Early stopping and best checkpoint selection strictly monitor `val_geneeffect_loss` `[docs/specs/2026-09-06-modular-joint-training-plan.md:19-21]`.

For deep technical details, see [Trainer Loop and Objective](#4.1).

Sources: `docs/specs/2026-09-06-modular-joint-training-design.md:68-94`, `src/training/trainer.py:53-118`

---

## 4.2 Configuration and CLI

Configurations are strictly specified via YAML files such as `configs/geneeffect_joint.yaml` `[tests/test_joint_cli.py:16-17]`. The configuration loader enforces schema bounds and rejects missing or unknown keys to prevent silent misconfigurations `[tests/test_joint_cli.py:56-65]`. Command-line interfaces like `src.train` and `src.evaluate` handle execution entrypoints and parameter overrides without importing heavy libraries unnecessarily during help commands `[tests/test_joint_cli.py:80-99]`.

```mermaid
graph TD
    sub6["NaturalLanguageSpace: Configuration and CLI"] -->|ControlledBy| code6["CodeEntitySpace: Parsers"]
    code6 --> LC[src/experiments/config.py]
    code6 --> TCLI[src/train.py]
    code6 --> ECLI[src/evaluate.py]
    
    LC -->|"load_config & validate_config"| Yaml[configs/geneeffect_joint.yaml]
    TCLI -->|"parse_args"| Run[run_training]
```
Sources: `tests/test_joint_cli.py:16-65`, `docs/specs/2026-09-06-modular-joint-training-plan.md:56`

For details, see [Configuration and CLI](#4.2).

Sources: `tests/test_joint_cli.py:16-99`, `docs/specs/2026-09-06-modular-joint-training-plan.md:56`

---

## 4.3 Checkpointing, Resume and Distributed Execution

Distributed execution leverages `Accelerate` and Distributed Data Parallel (DDP) wrappers to coordinate multi-rank training over PyTorch `[src/training/trainer.py:171-176, tests/test_joint_distributed.py:32-51]`. Checkpointing utilities (`src/training/checkpoint.py`) perform strict state loads, capturing optimizer states, RNG states, and training progress to enable exact resume behavior `[tests/test_joint_resume.py:26-95]`. HPC orchestration scripts (`hpc/run.sh`) manage large-scale resource provisioning and execution `[docs/specs/2026-09-06-modular-joint-training-plan.md:56]`.

For complete architectural details, see [Checkpointing, Resume and Distributed Execution](#4.3).

Sources: `src/training/trainer.py:171-176`, `tests/test_joint_distributed.py:32-51`, `tests/test_joint_resume.py:26-95`

---

## 4.4 Performance Profiling and Throughput

System throughput and memory utilization are continuously evaluated using diagnostic profiling probes (`profile_joint.py`) `[docs/specs/2026-09-06-modular-joint-training-design.md:115-117]`. Profiling results drive optimizations such as scaled batch sizing per rank (e.g., dependency batch size of 1024) to maximize GPU core efficiency across large cohorts `[docs/specs/2026-09-06-modular-joint-training-design.md:115-117]`.

For profiling metrics and diagnosis guides, see [Performance Profiling and Throughput](#4.4).

Sources: `docs/specs/2026-09-06-modular-joint-training-design.md:115-117`

# Page: Trainer Loop and Objective

# Trainer Loop and Objective

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/train.py](src/train.py)
- [src/training/trainer.py](src/training/trainer.py)
- [tests/test_joint_distributed.py](tests/test_joint_distributed.py)
- [tests/test_joint_resume.py](tests/test_joint_resume.py)
- [tests/test_joint_training.py](tests/test_joint_training.py)

</details>



The trainer loop and objective system orchestrates joint optimization of GeneEffect dependency prediction and single-cell response replay. This module manages parameter partitioning, gradient scaling, mixed-precision autocasting, distributed metric reduction via Hugging Face `accelerate`, and validation-driven early stopping based on validation GeneEffect loss.

Sources: `src/training/trainer.py:1-176](), `tests/test_joint_training.py:1-190]()

---

## Optimizer Partitioning and Parameter Groups

The optimizer configuration partitions model parameters into three distinct groups corresponding to the STATE backbone, the ESM2 perturbation adapter, and the prediction head. `make_optimizer` inspects `model` and constructs a `torch.optim.AdamW` optimizer with group-specific learning rates and shared weight decay [src/training/trainer.py:31-50]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    subcode ["Code Entities"]
        Model["model"] --> StateMod["model.backbone.state_adapter"]
        Model --> AdapterMod["model.backbone.perturbations"]
        Model --> HeadMod["model.head"]
        
        StateMod --> GroupState["Group: state (lr: train.state_learning_rate)"]
        AdapterMod --> GroupAdapter["Group: adapter (lr: train.adapter_learning_rate)"]
        HeadMod --> GroupHead["Group: head (lr: train.head_learning_rate)"]
        
        GroupState --> Opt["torch.optim.AdamW"]
        GroupAdapter --> Opt
        GroupHead --> Opt
    end
```
*Figure 1: Parameter partitioning flow from model components to optimizer groups.*

Sources: `src/training/trainer.py:31-50]()

---

## The Training Update Step (`train_update`)

The core gradient-update iteration is executed by `train_update`. It accepts dependency and optional response batches, performs a forward pass under mixed precision, computes joint losses, executes backpropagation with gradient clipping, and applies optimizer steps [src/training/trainer.py:53-117]().

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Trainer as "fit()"
    participant Update as "train_update()"
    participant Model as "model()"
    participant Loss as "Loss Functions"
    participant Acc as "accelerator"

    Trainer->>Update: "dependency_batch, response_batch, config, accelerator"
    Update->>Acc: "Device transfer & autocast()"
    Acc->>Model: "forward(conditions, response=response_input)"
    Model-->>Update: "output (delta_hat, response_predicted)"
    Update->>Loss: "geneeffect_loss(delta_hat, residual, valid)"
    alt response_batch is not None
        Update->>Loss: "response_terms(response_predicted, response_batch)"
    end
    Update->>Acc: "backward(total)"
    Acc->>Acc: "clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), 1.0)"
    Update->>Update: "optimizer.step(), optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)"
    Update->>Acc: "accelerator.reduce(values, reduction='mean')"
    Acc-->>Update: "Averaged train metrics dict"
```
*Figure 2: Execution sequence of a single training update step.*

### Implementation Mechanics

1. **Device Placement and Input Conversion**: Batches are moved to the target `accelerator.device` [src/training/trainer.py:59-61](). Response inputs are filtered into `ResponseForwardBatch` structures [src/training/trainer.py:62-66]().
2. **Forward Autocast**: Model execution is wrapped in `accelerator.autocast()` context [src/training/trainer.py:67-68]().
3. **Loss Aggregation**: Dependency loss (`geneeffect_loss`) is computed on residual targets [src/training/trainer.py:69-71](). If a response replay batch is present, `response_terms` calculates mean-delta MSE and energy distance, scaled by `response_weight` [src/training/trainer.py:74-78]().
4. **Gradient Clipping and Optimization**: Non-finite loss validation triggers explicit failure [src/training/trainer.py:79-80](). Backpropagation runs through `accelerator.backward()`, followed by gradient norm clipping at `1.0` [src/training/trainer.py:84-85]().
5. **Distributed Reduction**: Loss values across ranks are averaged using `accelerator.reduce` before returning logging metrics [src/training/trainer.py:93-117]().

Sources: `src/training/trainer.py:53-117](), `tests/test_joint_training.py:1-190]()

---

## Objective Formulation and Loss Components

The joint training objective combines dependency prediction error with single-cell response distributional alignment:

$$\mathcal{L}_{\text{total}} = \mathcal{L}_{\text{geneeffect}} + \lambda_{\text{response}} \left( \mathcal{L}_{\text{delta\_mse}} + \mathcal{L}_{\text{energy}} \right)$$

- **GeneEffect Loss ($\mathcal{L}_{\text{geneeffect}}$)**: Evaluated via Huber-style or customized robust regression on valid target pairs (`dependency_batch.residual`) [src/training/trainer.py:69-71]().
- **Response Replay Losses**: When active based on `response_interval` cadence, `response_terms` computes:
  - `mean_delta_mse`: Mean squared error of predicted versus observed single-cell response changes [src/training/trainer.py:77]().
  - `energy_distance`: Distributional discrepancy metric between predicted and observed response sets [src/training/trainer.py:78]().

Sources: `src/training/trainer.py:69-78](), `src/model/losses.py:1](), `src/model/response.py:1]()

---

## Training Orchestration (`fit`) and Early Stopping

The `fit` function manages epoch loops, startup standardizer fitting, checkpoint loading/saving, and state restoration [src/training/trainer.py:130-176]().

### Early Stopping and Checkpoint Selection

- **Validation Metric**: Model selection and patience tracking operate strictly on validation GeneEffect loss (`val_geneeffect_loss`), avoiding train-set overfitting interference [tests/test_joint_training.py:128-138]().
- **State Persistence**: Checkpoints (`best.pt` and `last.pt`) record optimizer states, AMP scaling states, RNG states, and training progression metrics via `TrainState` [src/training/trainer.py:17-22]().
- **DDP Configuration**: Distributed Data Parallel handles dynamic parameters via `find_unused_parameters = True` to support conditional auxiliary heads [src/training/trainer.py:171-174]().

Sources: `src/training/trainer.py:130-176](), `tests/test_joint_resume.py:1-162]()

---

# Configuration and CLI

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

This section covers the configuration system and Command Line Interfaces (CLIs) for the joint GeneEffect prediction and response-replay training pipeline. It details the structure of `configs/geneeffect_joint.yaml`, the strict schema validation enforcement implemented in `src/experiments/config.py`, the execution entrypoints (`src/train.py` and `src/evaluate.py`), and the launcher integration tests in `tests/test_joint_cli.py`.

---

## 1. Configuration Schema (`configs/geneeffect_joint.yaml`)

The joint training protocol relies on a single comprehensive YAML configuration file, `configs/geneeffect_joint.yaml`. The schema is partitioned into discrete logical groups: `seeds`, `train`, `selection`, `features`, `model`, `preparation`, and `paths`, alongside top-level parameters (`precision`, `output_root`, `prepared_root`).

```yaml
seeds: {train: 0, collator: 0, projection: 0}
train:
  max_epochs: 50
  patience: 5
  dependency_batch_size: 1024
  response_batch_size: 64
  response_interval: 4
  response_weight: 1.0
  state_learning_rate: 0.000001
  adapter_learning_rate: 0.00001
  head_learning_rate: 0.0001
  weight_decay: 0.01
selection: {metric: val_geneeffect_loss, mode: min}
precision: bf16
output_root: outputs/geneeffect_joint
prepared_root: data/geneeffect_joint/v1
...
```

Sources: [configs/geneeffect_joint.yaml:1-58]()

---

## 2. Strict Configuration Validation (`src/experiments/config.py`)

Configuration parsing is handled by `src/experiments/config.py`, which defines `load_config` and `validate_config`. Validation is executed strictly without opening input files or importing `torch`, enabling fast CLI help and boundary checking.

### Key Validation Rules
- **Schema Conformity**: Missing or unknown keys within any group (`_GROUPS`) or top-level field trigger a `ValueError` [src/experiments/config.py:41-48]().
- **Type Safety**: Boolean flags (such as `model.head_blocks`) must be real booleans; string paths must be non-empty strings [src/experiments/config.py:62-71]().
- **Head Block Constraint**: At least one head block (`use_delta_proj`, `use_s`, `use_q_sc`, `use_e_g`, `use_z_c`) must be enabled [src/experiments/config.py:64-65]().
- **Domain Constraints**: Learning rates, batch sizes, and percentiles are verified for finite numerical bounds and expected domains (e.g., `train.response_batch_size` must be divisible by 4, `train.response_interval` must equal `4`) [src/experiments/config.py:115-118]().
- **Fixed Seeds**: Base seeds (`seeds.train`, `seeds.collator`, `seeds.projection`) are strictly locked to `0` [src/experiments/config.py:76-78]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["load_config"] --> B["yaml.safe_load"]
    B --> C["validate_config"]
    C --> D["_keys checking _GROUPS"]
    D --> E["Head blocks boolean & non-empty check"]
    E --> F["Numerical & domain bounds check"]
    F --> G["Return validated dict"]

    style A fill:#fff,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
    style G fill:#fff,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
```
*Figure 1: Configuration Loading and Strict Validation Flow*

Sources: [src/experiments/config.py:1-136]()

---

## 3. Training and Evaluation CLIs (`src/train.py`, `src/evaluate.py`)

The codebase exposes two primary entrypoint scripts for executing experiments and inspecting saved checkpoints.

### Training CLI (`src/train.py` / `src/experiments/geneeffect.py`)
`src/train.py` parses arguments (`--run-id` or `--resume`) and dispatches control to `run_training` in `src/experiments/geneeffect.py`. 
- **Initialization**: Sets up the run directory (`output_root / run_id`), writes `run.json` containing revision hashes, seeds, environment stats (Python, PyTorch, Accelerate, device), and copies the validated configuration [src/experiments/geneeffect.py:96-125]().
- **Execution & Resuming**: Loads inputs via `load_inputs`, constructs the joint model via `build_joint_model` or restores it via `_restore_model`, and passes control to the trainer loop (`fit`) [src/experiments/geneeffect.py:137-150]().

### Evaluation CLI (`src/evaluate.py`)
`src/evaluate.py` provides independent evaluation over saved checkpoints (`--checkpoint`, `--split train|val|test`), invoking `evaluate_checkpoint` without triggering optimizer steps [src/evaluate.py:1-23](), [src/experiments/geneeffect.py:179-188]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    subicon["CLI Entrypoints"]

    subicon --> E["src.evaluate.main"]
    
    T --> GT["src.experiments.geneeffect.run_training"]
    E --> GE["src.experiments.geneeffect.evaluate_checkpoint"]
    
    GT --> LI["src.data.prepared.load_inputs"]
    GT --> JM["src.model.initialization.build_joint_model"]
    GT --> FT["src.training.trainer.fit"]
    
    GE --> EV["src.eval.geneeffect.evaluate_model"]

    style T fill:#fff,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
    style E fill:#fff,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
    style GT fill:#fff,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
    style GE fill:#fff,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
```
*Figure 2: CLI Command Dispatch and Execution Architecture*

Sources: [src/evaluate.py:1-23](), [src/experiments/geneeffect.py:61-188]()

---

## 4. Launcher and CLI Unit Tests (`tests/test_joint_cli.py`)

Testing safeguards are codified in `tests/test_joint_cli.py`. These tests validate configuration boundaries and execution behavior without requiring heavy GPU resources or full model initialization where possible.

- **`test_approved_defaults_and_conflicts`**: Ensures default values match specification and mutations to constrained fields correctly raise `ValueError` [tests/test_joint_cli.py:16-37]().
- **`test_ablation_flags_require_real_booleans`**: Verifies that integer or string representations of booleans (e.g., `0`, `"false"`) in `head_blocks` are rejected [tests/test_joint_cli.py:39-45]().
- **`test_all_disabled_head_is_rejected`**: Guards against fully disabled head configurations [tests/test_joint_cli.py:47-53]().
- **`test_help_does_not_import_torch`**: Executes module `--help` runs via `runpy` and asserts that `torch` is not loaded into `sys.modules`, ensuring lightweight CLI responsiveness [tests/test_joint_cli.py:77-99]().
- **`test_missing_cache_training_fails_without_raw_rebuild`**: Asserts that running training against missing prepared caches fails cleanly with a `FileNotFoundError` pointing to preparation instructions rather than silently falling back to raw assembly [tests/test_joint_cli.py:122-148]().

Sources: [tests/test_joint_cli.py:1-183]()

# Page: Checkpointing, Resume and Distributed Execution

# Checkpointing, Resume and Distributed Execution

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [hpc/run.sh](hpc/run.sh)
- [src/training/checkpoint.py](src/training/checkpoint.py)
- [src/training/distributed.py](src/training/distributed.py)
- [tests/test_distributed.py](tests/test_distributed.py)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope
This page documents the joint training infrastructure's state management, fault tolerance, and distributed execution mechanisms. It covers strict checkpoint serialization and resumption (`src/training/checkpoint.py`), multi-rank distributed data parallel (DDP) safety and synchronization (`src/training/distributed.py`), unit test coverage for DDP invariants (`tests/test_distributed.py`), and job orchestration through the HPC entrypoint script (`hpc/run.sh`).

Sources: `src/training/checkpoint.py`, `src/training/distributed.py`, `tests/test_distributed.py`, `hpc/run.sh`

---

## 1. Checkpoint Architecture and State Management (`checkpoint.py`)

The checkpoint system manages epoch-boundary persistence, tracking validation loss metrics, and ensuring complete reproducibility across resume cycles.

### Key Data Structures and Functions
- **`TrainState`**: A dataclass tracking optimization progress (`src/training/checkpoint.py:16-23`):
  - `next_epoch`: The index of the next training epoch to execute.
  - `global_step`: Total optimizer update steps performed.
  - `best_loss`: Best recorded validation metric (`val_geneeffect_loss`), initialized to `math.inf`.
  - `best_epoch`: Epoch index where `best_loss` was achieved.
  - `bad_epochs`: Count of consecutive epochs without validation improvement (used for early stopping).
- **`record_validation()`**: Evaluates epoch metrics against `val_geneeffect_loss` and updates `TrainState` strictly on GeneEffect loss decrease (`src/training/checkpoint.py:25-38`).
- **`capture_rng_state()` & `restore_rng_state()`**: Isolate and serialize random number generator states across Python `random`, `numpy.random` (converting MT19937 state words into tensor-compatible representations), `torch`, and accelerator-specific devices (`cuda` or `mps`) (`src/training/checkpoint.py:41-65`).
- **`save_checkpoint()`**: Collects RNG states from all active distributed ranks via `torch.distributed.all_gather_object`, unwraps the model via `accelerator.unwrap_model()`, serializes model weights, projection states, normalizer states, optimizer states, AMP scalers, and rank-specific RNG states into an atomic `.tmp` file before renaming it to the final destination path (`src/training/checkpoint.py:67-106`).
- **`load_checkpoint()`**: Performs CPU-side loading (`weights_only=True`), validates all required keys against a strict schema, and verifies that the saved world size matches the expected number of RNG states (`src/training/checkpoint.py:108-130`).

### Checkpoint Save and Load Flow

```mermaid
graph TD
    sub0[""Save Checkpoint Workflow""]
    A["capture_rng_state"] --> B["all_gather_object"]
    B --> C["accelerator.unwrap_model"]
    C --> D["Construct Payload Dict"]
    D --> E["torch.save to .tmp"]
    E --> F["Atomic rename to Path"]

    sub1[""Load Checkpoint Workflow""]
    G["torch.load with weights_only=True"] --> H["Validate Required Keys"]
    H --> I["Validate World Size & RNG States"]
    I --> J["Instantiate TrainState"]
    J --> K["Return Saved Dict"]

    style A fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style G fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
```
Sources: `src/training/checkpoint.py`

---

## 2. Distributed Coordination and DDP Invariants (`distributed.py`)

Multi-rank execution in joint training requires strict device validation and collective error propagation to prevent silent deadlocks or desynchronization across ranks.

### Key Functions
- **`require_distinct_devices()`**: Validates device assignments across all processes when `accelerator.num_processes > 1` (`src/training/distributed.py:10-39`). It gathers local device representations using `torch.distributed.all_gather_object` and asserts that either all ranks run on CPU/Gloo or all ranks are assigned distinct CUDA device indices.
- **`raise_rank_errors()`**: Collects error states across ranks prior to dependent collectives or optimizer updates, raising a unified `RuntimeError` if any rank reported a failure (`src/training/distributed.py:41-49`).
- **`run_rank_zero_or_raise()`**: Executes a callback function exclusively on the main process (`accelerator.is_main_process`), captures any raised exceptions, and broadcasts the failure summary and stack trace to all worker ranks using `torch.distributed.broadcast_object_list` (`src/training/distributed.py:51-72`).

### Distributed Guard Architecture

```mermaid
graph TD
    sub2[""Distributed Safety Guard System""]
    AA["require_distinct_devices"] --> AB["all_gather_object device tuples"]
    AB --> AC{"Distinct CUDA or CPU?"}
    AC -- No --> AD["Raise RuntimeError"]
    AC -- Yes --> AE["Proceed Execution"]

    AF["run_rank_zero_or_raise"] --> AG["is_main_process action"]
    AG -- Exception --> AH["Capture Traceback & Summary"]
    AH --> AI["broadcast_object_list to all ranks"]
    AI --> AJ["Raise Unified RuntimeError"]

    style AA fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style AF fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
```
Sources: `src/training/distributed.py`

### DDP Unit Testing (`tests/test_distributed.py`)
The test suite utilizes a mock accelerator (`FakeAccelerator`) and monkeypatches `torch.distributed.all_gather_object` to validate distributed safety rules without initializing a real process group (`tests/test_distributed.py:1-35`):
- `test_require_distinct_devices_single_process_is_noop`: Confirms no collectives execute for single-process training (`tests/test_distributed.py:36-43`).
- `test_require_distinct_devices_raises_on_duplicate_cuda_index`: Guards against duplicate GPU assignments (`tests/test_distributed.py:45-54`).
- `test_require_distinct_devices_raises_on_non_cuda_rank`: Ensures homogeneous device assignment across workers (`tests/test_distributed.py:56-65`).
- `test_run_rank_zero_or_raise_reraises_rank_zero_failure`: Verifies exception propagation from rank zero to worker nodes (`tests/test_distributed.py:102-110`).

Sources: `src/training/distributed.py`, `tests/test_distributed.py`

---

## 3. HPC Job Orchestration (`hpc/run.sh`)

Job execution across single-node and multi-GPU environments is orchestrated by `hpc/run.sh`. The script manages environment resolution, accelerator configuration, and subcommand routing.

### CLI Commands and Workflow
`hpc/run.sh` supports the following primary subcommands (`hpc/run.sh:4-15`):
- `prepare`: Data preparation entrypoint (`src.experiments.prepare`).
- `train`: Joint training execution (`src.train`).
- `test`: Evaluation entrypoint against specified checkpoints (`src.evaluate`).
- `p1a`, `p1b`, `p1c`: Diagnostic experiment pipeline stages.

### GPU Detection and Launch Orchestration
For the `train` command, `hpc/run.sh` dynamically queries visible GPUs using PyTorch, configures Hugging Face `accelerate`, and launches training with mixed precision (`bf16`) (`hpc/run.sh:34-44`):
1. Detects available worker devices: `workers=$("$python_bin" -c 'import torch; print(torch.cuda.device_count())')` (`hpc/run.sh:36`).
2. Validates that at least one GPU is visible.
3. Constructs launch arguments for `accelerate.commands.launch`, appending `--multi_gpu` if `workers > 1` (`hpc/run.sh:41-43`).

```mermaid
graph TD
    sub3[""HPC Orchestration and Launch Pipeline""]
    BA["hpc/run.sh train CONFIG"] --> BB["Detect CUDA device_count"]
    BB --> BC{"workers >= 1?"}
    BC -- No --> BD["Exit with Error"]
    BC -- Yes --> BE["Configure accelerate launch"]
    BE --> BF{"workers > 1?"}
    BF -- Yes --> BG["Add --multi_gpu flag"]
    BF -- No --> BH["Single GPU launch"]
    BG --> BI["exec python_bin -m accelerate.commands.launch"]
    BH --> BI
    BI --> BJ["Execute src.train"]

    style BA fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style BI fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
```
Sources: `hpc/run.sh`

---

# Performance Profiling and Throughput

This page covers the system performance profiling infrastructure, throughput diagnosis procedures, vectorization enhancements, and scaling outcomes for the joint GeneEffect and response-replay training architecture. The implementation centers around bounded profiling harnesses (`src/experiments/profile_joint.py`), adapter-level batching optimizations (`src/model/state.py`), and empirical diagnosis records spanning single-GPU and distributed (DDP) executions on NVIDIA H20 hardware.

---

## 1. The Bounded Profiling Probe (`profile_joint.py`)

To evaluate training iterations without committing checkpoints or running full multi-day training epochs, the codebase provides a specialized timing and profiling probe in `src/experiments/profile_joint.py`. 

The script parses command-line arguments configuring the target YAML file, output path, step count (default 64, strictly required to be a positive multiple of 4 to sample regular and response-replay steps consistently), and an optional dependency batch size override [src/experiments/profile_joint.py:25-39](). It enforces execution under a CUDA accelerator context and disables multi-worker operator profiling unless running a single worker process [src/experiments/profile_joint.py:40-47]().

The probe initialization flow executes the following sequence:
1. Loads prepared inputs using `load_inputs` [src/experiments/profile_joint.py:51]().
2. Instantiates the joint model via `build_joint_model` and transfers it to the accelerator device [src/experiments/profile_joint.py:52]().
3. Fits startup normalization tensors through `fit_startup_standardizer` [src/experiments/profile_joint.py:53-56]().
4. Wraps the model and optimizer with `accelerator.prepare` [src/experiments/profile_joint.py:57-58]().
5. Constructs training and response replay iterators via `make_training_loaders` [src/experiments/profile_joint.py:60]().

During the timed loop, update steps alternate between ordinary GeneEffect updates and response-replay updates (triggered every 4 steps) using `train_update` [src/experiments/profile_joint.py:64-70](). CUDA synchronization ensures accurate hardware timing, discarding the first 8 warmup steps before measuring median durations [src/experiments/profile_joint.py:72-82](). Peak allocated memory is queried via `torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated()` and aggregated across ranks using distributed all-reduce operations if `world_size > 1` [src/experiments/profile_joint.py:83-89]().

```mermaid
title "Natural Language Space to Code Entity Space: Profiling Probe Execution"
graph TD
    subgraph "Natural Language Space"
        NL_Init["H20 Hardware Initialization & Warmup"]
        NL_Step["Bounded Step Timing: Ordinary vs Replay"]
    end

    subgraph "Code Entity Space"
        CE_Config["src/experiments/config.load_config"]
        CE_Inputs["src/data/prepared.load_inputs"]
        CE_Model["src/model/initialization.build_joint_model"]
        CE_Norm["src/model/normalization.fit_startup_standardizer"]
        CE_Train["src/training/trainer.train_update"]
        CE_Profile["src/experiments/profile_joint.py:main"]
    end

    NL_Init --> CE_Profile
    CE_Profile --> CE_Config
    CE_Profile --> CE_Inputs
    CE_Profile --> CE_Model
    CE_Model --> CE_Norm
    NL_Step --> CE_Train
    CE_Profile --> CE_Train
```

Sources: `src/experiments/profile_joint.py`, `docs/results/2026-09-06-joint-throughput-diagnosis.md`

---

## 2. Throughput Diagnosis and Resident Input Optimizations

Initial baseline profiling on single-GPU H20 hardware revealed severe bottlenecks stemming from repeated CPU-to-GPU memory transfers of fixed input structures. Baseline profiling recorded 5,832 `memcpy` calls and 4,559 stream synchronizations across only four updates, where dependency transfers alone accounted for approximately 75 ms per update [docs/results/2026-09-06-joint-throughput-diagnosis.md:68-70]().

To mitigate this, several architectural shifts were introduced:
* **Resident Basal Inputs**: Datasets retain one sampled basal tensor per eligible `ModelID` directly on the worker device, allowing reuse across batches without triggering recurring host-to-device transfers [docs/results/2026-09-06-joint-throughput-diagnosis.md:76-78]().
* **Window Views**: Complete STATE windows leverage tensor views instead of allocating and transferring new index tensors per condition [docs/results/2026-09-06-joint-throughput-diagnosis.md:74-75]().

```mermaid
title "Natural Language Space to Code Entity Space: Resident Input Optimization"
graph TD
    subgraph "Natural Language Space"
        NL_Resident["Device-Resident Basal Tensors"]
        NL_Views["Zero-Copy Window Views"]
    end

    subgraph "Code Entity Space"
        CE_Load["src/data/prepared.load_inputs"]
        CE_Dataset["src/data/datasets.DependencyDataset"]
        CE_Adapter["src/model/state.StateForwardAdapter"]
        CE_Forward["src/model/state.StateForwardAdapter:forward_condition_chunks"]
    end

    NL_Resident --> CE_Dataset
    NL_Views --> CE_Adapter
    CE_Load --> CE_Dataset
    CE_Dataset --> CE_Forward
    CE_Adapter --> CE_Forward
```

Sources: `src/experiments/profile_joint.py`, `docs/results/2026-09-06-joint-throughput-diagnosis.md`

---

## 3. Vectorization and Kernel-Launch Minimization

Subsequent vectorization diagnostics identified further inefficiencies in dtype casting, perturbation expansion, and distance loss computations [docs/results/2026-09-06-joint-vectorization-diagnosis.md:1-16](). 

Key code-level vectorization improvements implemented in `src/model/state.py` and related response modules include:
* **Single FP32 Cast**: Low-precision STATE outputs (`torch.float16` or `torch.bfloat16`) are cast to `torch.float32` *once* at the boundary of `forward_condition_chunks` before splitting into condition views, eliminating redundant casting and backward cast overhead per chunk [src/model/state.py:125-129]().
* **Batched Perturbation Expansion**: Perturbations across multi-condition chunks are expanded as a single matrix operation in `forward_condition_chunks`, avoiding individual reduction kernels per chunk during gradient propagation [src/model/state.py:108-112]().
* **Response Distance Grouping**: Response bags are grouped by shape to enable batched distance computation kernels in `src/model/response.py`, reducing kernel launch counts and stream synchronizations [docs/results/2026-09-06-joint-vectorization-diagnosis.md:58-65]().

These optimizations reduced total kernel launches from 18,128 to 11,069 (a 38.9% reduction) and stream synchronizations by 19.3% [docs/results/2026-09-06-joint-vectorization-diagnosis.md:62-65]().

Sources: `src/model/state.py`, `docs/results/2026-09-06-joint-vectorization-diagnosis.md`

---

## 4. Empirical Performance and Scaling Results

Profiling probes and production logs document steady throughput improvements across successive optimization phases on NVIDIA H20 nodes (`apg3op6hp3v99-0`, 97871 MiB VRAM).

### Throughput and Memory Progression

| Implementation Phase | Revision | GPUs | Dependency Batch / Rank | Throughput (Rows/s) | Peak Allocated (GiB / rank) |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| Baseline | `7a79352` [docs/results/2026-09-06-joint-throughput-probes.json:8]() | 1 | 256 | 802 | 15.39 [docs/results/2026-09-06-joint-throughput-probes.json:16]() |
| Window Views | `abe57f0` [docs/results/2026-09-06-joint-throughput-probes.json:33]() | 1 | 256 | 849 | 15.31 [docs/results/2026-09-06-joint-throughput-probes.json:41]() |
| Resident Basal Inputs | `bbe4670` [docs/results/2026-09-06-joint-throughput-probes.json:83]() | 1 | 256 | 1,179 | 14.99 [docs/results/2026-09-06-joint-throughput-probes.json:91]() |
| Optimized DDP (2 GPUs) | `f3d6118` [docs/results/2026-09-06-joint-throughput-probes.json:108]() | 2 | 256 | 2,043 | 15.15 [docs/results/2026-09-06-joint-throughput-probes.json:116]() |
| Final Vectorization | `f73f4e0` [docs/results/2026-09-06-joint-vectorization-diagnosis.md:10]() | 2 | 256 | 2,230 | 15.16 [docs/results/2026-09-06-joint-vectorization-diagnosis.md:38]() |
| Batch 1024 Scaling | `36acbd0` [docs/results/2026-09-06-joint-batch1024.md:5]() | 2 | 1,024 | **2,867** | ~60.8 GiB (Occupancy) [docs/results/2026-09-06-joint-batch1024.md:49-53]() |

### Batch Size Scaling and Resource Utilization

Scaling the per-rank dependency batch size from 256 to 1024 (`outputs/geneeffect_joint/joint_seed0_20260906T174818Z_b1024/`) increased row throughput to **2,867 rows/second** while raising GPU compute utilization from ~76% to over **88–90%** across both H20 cards [docs/results/2026-09-06-joint-batch1024.md:43-52](). Observed allocator memory occupancy stabilized at approximately 62.3 GiB per card under batch 1024 [docs/results/2026-09-06-joint-batch1024.md:51-53]().

Sources: `docs/results/2026-09-06-joint-throughput-probes.json`, `docs/results/2026-09-06-joint-vectorization-diagnosis.md`, `docs/results/2026-09-06-joint-batch1024.md`

# Evaluation and Baselines

<details>

## Purpose and Scope

This page provides a high-level overview of the evaluation systems, metric definitions, and baseline controls used to assess gene perturbation predictions and response distributions within the codebase. The evaluation framework handles aligned-row GeneEffect scoring (measuring residual prediction performance across cell lines and genes) alongside distributional response metrics, while storing artifacts and running systematic baseline comparisons. 

For deep technical details, see the child pages:
- [GeneEffect and Response Metrics](#5.1)
- [Baseline Controls](#5.2)
- [Results Archive and Evidence](#5.3)

---

## 5.1 GeneEffect and Response Metrics

The evaluation infrastructure measures two primary prediction modalities: continuous GeneEffect residuals and single-cell response distributions. The module `src/eval/geneeffect.py` coordinates evaluation runs, metric gathering across parallel processes, and correlation aggregation [src/eval/geneeffect.py:1-53](). Simultaneously, `src/eval/response.py` evaluates single-cell response predictions using metrics like mean-delta MSE and energy distance [src/eval/response.py:1-59](). The underlying statistical operations, such as unit-level Pearson and Spearman correlations with strict minimum-observation thresholds, are housed in `src/eval/metrics.py` [src/eval/metrics.py:100-118]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    EvalModule[""Evaluation System""] --> GeneEffectEval[""src/eval/geneeffect.py""]
    EvalModule --> ResponseEval[""src/eval/response.py""]
    EvalModule --> MetricsEngine[""src/eval/metrics.py""]
    GeneEffectEval --> ComposeMetrics[""compose_metrics()""]
    ResponseEval --> AggregateResponse[""aggregate_response()""]
    MetricsEngine --> PerGeneSpearman[""macro_per_gene_spearman()""]
```
Sources: `src/eval/geneeffect.py:1-53`, `src/eval/response.py:1-60`, `src/eval/metrics.py:100-118`

For details, see [GeneEffect and Response Metrics](#5.1).

---

## 5.2 Baseline Controls

To contextualize the performance of the neural network architectures, the repository incorporates multiple analytical baseline controls. These range from simple unconditional predictors like gene-mean and copy-number priors to more sophisticated contextual models including nearest-line matching, context-PCA ridge regression, and tx1 GMM ridge baselines. These baselines provide rigorous lower bounds and calibration references for both GeneEffect and perturbation response predictions.

For details, see [Baseline Controls](#5.2).

---

## 5.3 Results Archive and Evidence

The evaluation and experimentation outputs are cataloged under the documentation and results hierarchy. This structure preserves joint-training evidence, multi-stage diagnostic outcomes from programs such as `exp05` and `exp13`, prior internal validation reports, and publication-ready figures.

```mermaid
graph TD
    Archive[""Results Archive""] --> DocResults[""docs/results/""]
    DocResults --> JointRunEvidence[""Joint Run Evidence""]
    DocResults --> ExpStages[""exp05/exp13 Stages""]
    DocResults --> VisualArtifacts[""Figures and Evidence""]
```
Sources: `docs/results`

For details, see [Results Archive and Evidence](#5.3).

# Page: GeneEffect and Response Metrics

# GeneEffect and Response Metrics

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/eval/geneeffect.py](src/eval/geneeffect.py)
- [src/eval/metrics.py](src/eval/metrics.py)
- [src/eval/response.py](src/eval/response.py)
- [tests/test_build_cell_line_geneeffect_226_split.py](tests/test_build_cell_line_geneeffect_226_split.py)
- [tests/test_joint_checkpoint.py](tests/test_joint_checkpoint.py)
- [tests/test_joint_evaluation.py](tests/test_joint_evaluation.py)
- [tests/test_residual_metrics.py](tests/test_residual_metrics.py)
- [tests/test_residual_target.py](tests/test_residual_target.py)
- [tests/test_run_r1_residual_ladder.py](tests/test_run_r1_residual_ladder.py)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope
This page documents the evaluation architecture, metrics, and residual target definitions located in `src/eval/geneeffect.py`, `src/eval/response.py`, `src/eval/metrics.py`, and `src/data/residual_target.py`. These modules provide row-aligned inference scoring, multi-axis correlation calculation (per-line and per-gene Spearman/Pearson), response distribution loss aggregation (mean-delta MSE and energy distance), and the immutable residual baseline framework.

Sources: `src/eval/geneeffect.py:1-31`, `src/eval/response.py:1-12`, `src/eval/metrics.py:1-35`

---

## GeneEffect Evaluation and Aggregation (`src/eval/geneeffect.py`)

The GeneEffect evaluation engine collects predictions across batched dependencies, computes Huber loss against residual targets, and gathers distributed outputs across ranks. 

### Key Classes and Functions
*   `EvalResult`: A dataclass encapsulating scalar metrics dictionaries, flat predictions dataframes, per-line metrics, per-gene metrics, and response metrics [src/eval/geneeffect.py:23-30]().
*   `compose_metrics`: Combines GeneEffect and response losses using a configured `response_weight`, validating finiteness across all metrics [src/eval/geneeffect.py:32-53]().
*   `_dependency_rows`: Computes forward passes (`model(batch.conditions).delta_hat`), extracts predictions, maps residues back to raw GeneEffect space (`delta + gene_mean`), and filters valid score rows [src/eval/geneeffect.py:56-91]().
*   `_gather_batch_rows`: Handles distributed gather operations using `accelerator.gather_for_metrics`, propagating rank-local evaluation failures [src/eval/geneeffect.py:94-110]().
*   `aggregate_geneeffect`: Derives pair errors, root-mean-square error (RMSE), mean absolute error (MAE), standard deviation ratios, and both correlation axes (`per_line` and `per_gene`) from the gathered frame [src/eval/geneeffect.py:156-177]().

### Evaluation Pipeline Architecture

```mermaid
graph TD
  DependencyBatch["DependencyBatch"] -->|model(batch.conditions)| ModelForward["Model Forward Pass"]
  ModelForward -->|delta_hat| DependencyRows["_dependency_rows"]
  DependencyRows -->|Gather Ranks| GatherBatch["_gather_batch_rows"]
  GatherBatch -->|DataFrame Rows| AggregateGE["aggregate_geneeffect"]
  AggregateGE --> EvalRes["EvalResult"]
```
Sources: `src/eval/geneeffect.py:23-177`

---

## Response Metrics and Aggregation (`src/eval/response.py`)

Response metrics evaluate distributional shifts on held-out single-cell expression bags.

### Key Functions
*   `response_rows`: Evaluates held-out conditions using the unwrapped evaluation-only backbone via `predict_bags` and `response_terms` [src/eval/response.py:13-36]().
*   `aggregate_response`: Averages response terms (`mean_delta_mse` and `energy_distance`) within each `model_id`, then aggregates equally across four distinct evaluation anchors (`anchors`) [src/eval/response.py:39-59](). It computes `response_loss` as the sum of mean MSE and mean energy distance.

Sources: `src/eval/response.py:1-60`

---

## Statistical Metrics and Correlation Axes (`src/eval/metrics.py`)

The metrics module defines two distinct correlation axes for dependency prediction performance: **per-line** (predicting gene effects across genes within a given cell line) and **per-gene** (predicting gene effects across cell lines for a given gene).

### Key Classes and Functions
*   `MacroPerGeneSpearman`: Named tuple tracking `macro` mean, `per_gene` series, `n_scored`, and `n_undefined` [src/eval/metrics.py:15-31]().
*   `macro_per_gene_spearman`: Computes macro per-gene Spearman across contexts using tensor shapes `[n_genes, n_contexts]` [src/eval/metrics.py:33-94]().
*   `_unit_spearman`: Evaluates Spearman rank correlation on finite pairs for a single unit, returning `nan` (never `0.0` or raised exceptions) if fewer than `MIN_OBSERVATIONS` (3) finite pairs exist or if truth/prediction vectors are constant [src/eval/metrics.py:120-148]().
*   `score_predictions`: High-level driver computing residual scores, macro metrics, and shuffle controls [tests/test_residual_metrics.py:20-27]().

### Metric Computation Flow

```mermaid
graph TD
  PredictionFrame["DataFrame truth and pred"] --> GroupUnit["groupby unit_col model_id or gene_symbol"]
  GroupUnit --> FilterFinite["Filter finite pairs"]
  FilterFinite --> CheckValid["Check MIN_OBSERVATIONS and variance"]
  CheckValid -->|Valid| ComputeSpearman["scipy.stats.spearmanr"]
  CheckValid -->|Constant/TooFew| ReturnNaN["Return NaN"]
  ComputeSpearman --> SeriesOut["pd.Series per unit"]
  ReturnNaN --> SeriesOut
  SeriesOut --> MacroAgg["Macro Nanmean Aggregation"]
```
Sources: `src/eval/metrics.py:15-184`, `tests/test_residual_metrics.py:20-27`

---

## Residual Targets and Baseline Framework (`src/data/residual_target.py` & `src/baselines/residual.py`)

To prevent models from exploiting gene-mean baselines, GeneEffect targets are formulated as residuals relative to historical gene means.

### Key Components
*   `fit_gene_means`: Computes gene means ($\mu_g$) strictly from training lines (`train_lines`), ensuring held-out validation or test lines never leak into the mean calculation [tests/test_residual_target.py:21-42]().
*   `build_residual_targets`: Materializes `ResidualTargets`, combining raw `gene_effect`, fitted `gene_mean`, and computed `residual` ($y_{g,c} - \hat{\mu}_g$) [tests/test_residual_target.py:47-53]().
*   `run_r1_ladder`: Executes the numerical baseline ladder (including gene-mean, copy-prior, nearest-line, context-PCA-ridge, and tx1 GMM ridge) across specified outer folds or leave-one-line-out (`lolo`) schemes [tests/test_run_r1_residual_ladder.py:144-146]().

Sources: `tests/test_residual_target.py:9-55`, `tests/test_run_r1_residual_ladder.py:23-28`

---

# Page: Baseline Controls

# Baseline Controls

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [docs/04-sl-ranking-protocol.md](docs/04-sl-ranking-protocol.md)
- [docs/results/tx1_gmm_ridge_seed0/README.md](docs/results/tx1_gmm_ridge_seed0/README.md)
- [docs/results/tx1_gmm_ridge_seed0/evidence.json](docs/results/tx1_gmm_ridge_seed0/evidence.json)
- [docs/specs/2026-09-07-tx1-gmm-ridge-design.md](docs/specs/2026-09-07-tx1-gmm-ridge-design.md)
- [docs/specs/2026-09-07-tx1-gmm-ridge-plan.md](docs/specs/2026-09-07-tx1-gmm-ridge-plan.md)
- [src/baselines/tx1_gmm.py](src/baselines/tx1_gmm.py)
- [src/experiments/tx1_gmm_ridge.py](src/experiments/tx1_gmm_ridge.py)
- [tests/test_tx1_gmm_ridge.py](tests/test_tx1_gmm_ridge.py)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope
This page documents the baseline control models implemented in the gene-perturbation prediction codebase. These baselines provide rigorous lower and upper performance bounds against which the full STATE backbone and joint neural network architectures are evaluated. The scope covers five primary control strategies: the context-blind **gene-mean** control, the **copy-prior** structural control, the **nearest-line** non-parametric neighbor control, the **context-PCA-ridge** linear baseline (using either HVG or Tx1 features), and the recently implemented **Tx1 GMM ridge baseline** (`Tx1GMMRidge`).

---

## 1. Overview of Baseline Architecture and Strategy
Baselines isolate whether learned deep representations (such as the STATE backbone and ESM2 perturbation adapters) add predictive value over simpler statistical summaries of basal cellular state and gene identity. 

The baseline controls operate on shared prepared inputs (`PreparedInputs`), enforcing strict separation between training cell lines and held-out validation/test splits to prevent data leakage.

```mermaid
graph TD
    sub-graph-Inputs["Input Data Layer"]
    InputData["PreparedInputs object\nsrc/data/prepared.py"] --> BaselineSelector["Baseline Dispatcher\nsrc/experiments/baselines.py"]

    sub-graph-Baselines["Baseline Implementations"]
    BaselineSelector --> GeneMean["Gene-Mean Control\nPan-essential mean"]
    BaselineSelector --> CopyPrior["Copy-Prior Control\nStructural CNV prior"]
    BaselineSelector --> NearestLine["Nearest-Line Control\nCosine/Euclidean distance"]
    BaselineSelector --> ContextPCA["Context-PCA-Ridge\nsrc/baselines/"]
    BaselineSelector --> Tx1GMM["Tx1 GMM Ridge\nsrc/baselines/tx1_gmm.py"]

    Tx1GMM --> GMMFit["GaussianMixture fit\nK=64 diagonal"]
    GMMFit --> FeatureExtract["Context Feature Vector\noccupancy, entropy, nll"]
    FeatureExtract --> RidgeFit["Per-Gene Ridge Regression\nalpha=1.0"]

    Sources: "Sources: src/experiments/tx1_gmm_ridge.py:74-130, src/baselines/tx1_gmm.py:70-167"
```

Sources: `src/experiments/tx1_gmm_ridge.py:74-130`, `src/baselines/tx1_gmm.py:70-167`

---

## 2. Implemented Baseline Classes and Functions

### Tx1 GMM Ridge Baseline (`Tx1GMMRidge`)
The `Tx1GMMRidge` model is defined in `src/baselines/tx1_gmm.py` [src/baselines/tx1_gmm.py:19-199]() and orchestrated via `src/experiments/tx1_gmm_ridge.py` [src/experiments/tx1_gmm_ridge.py:1-175](). It fits a global cell-dimension `StandardScaler` and a diagonal `GaussianMixture` model ($K=64$) on equal numbers of single-cell rows sampled from each labeled training line.

Key functions and classes include:
- `Tx1GMMRidge.fit(inputs, *, n_components)`: Validates splits, balances cell counts across training lines without replacement, fits scalers and the GMM, extracts context feature matrices, and fits per-gene `Ridge(alpha=1.0)` models [src/baselines/tx1_gmm.py:70-167]().
- `Tx1GMMRidge._features(bag, cell_scaler, gmm)`: Computes posterior responsibilities, occupancy probabilities, occupancy entropy, effective component count, mean assignment confidence, and mean negative log-likelihood (`nll`) for a given cell bag [src/baselines/tx1_gmm.py:42-58]().
- `evaluate_model(model, inputs, *, split)`: Computes evaluation metrics (Huber loss, RMSE, residual Pearson/Spearman correlations, and macro per-gene SD ratios) for train or validation sets [src/experiments/tx1_gmm_ridge.py:8-53]().

Sources: `src/baselines/tx1_gmm.py:19-200`, `src/experiments/tx1_gmm_ridge.py:1-176`

---

## 3. Detailed Data Flow and Fitting Mechanics

The baseline execution pipeline for GMM ridge proceeds through strict preparation, feature extraction, and target residualization steps.

```mermaid
graph TD
    Load["load_config & load_inputs\nsrc/experiments/tx1_gmm_ridge.py"] --> SampleCells["Sample balanced cells\nmin cells per bag, seed=0"]
    SampleCells --> ScaleCells["Fit global cell StandardScaler\nsrc/baselines/tx1_gmm.py"]
    ScaleCells --> FitGMM["Fit GaussianMixture K=64\ndiag covariance, reg_covar=1e-4"]
    FitGMM --> ExtractContext["Compute context features\nEntropy, NLL, Conf, Occupancy"]
    ExtractContext --> ScaleContext["Fit context StandardScaler"]
    ScaleContext --> RidgeReg["Fit Ridge alpha=1.0 per gene\ntarget - gene_mean"]
    RidgeReg --> Export["Export model.joblib & metrics\nsrc/experiments/tx1_gmm_ridge.py"]

    Sources: "Sources: src/baselines/tx1_gmm.py:70-167, docs/specs/2026-09-07-tx1-gmm-ridge-design.md:1-37"
```

Sources: `src/baselines/tx1_gmm.py:70-167`, `docs/specs/2026-09-07-tx1-gmm-ridge-design.md:1-37`

---

## 4. Empirical Performance and Evaluation Results

Empirical comparisons between baselines are archived under `docs/results/tx1_gmm_ridge_seed0/` [docs/results/tx1_gmm_ridge_seed0/README.md:1-69](). The validation set comprises 479,084 observed `(ModelID, gene_symbol)` pairs across 27 validation lines with 4,447 variable genes.

| Method | Huber ↓ | RMSE ↓ | Residual Pearson ↑ | Residual Spearman ↑ | Macro per-gene SD ratio |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Tx1 GMM64-ridge, $\alpha=1$ | 0.054734 | 0.344255 | 0.078027 | 0.081147 | 1.312647 |
| Tx1 PCA8-ridge, $\alpha=1$ | 0.016281 | 0.181303 | 0.132973 | 0.123286 | 0.272707 |
| HVG PCA8-ridge, $\alpha=1$ | 0.016451 | 0.182288 | 0.080383 | 0.087934 | 0.203722 |
| Gene mean | 0.016317 | 0.181596 | undefined | undefined | 0 |

As documented in `evidence.json` [docs/results/tx1_gmm_ridge_seed0/evidence.json:1-175](), the fixed GMM64 configuration exhibits a large training-to-validation gap (train Huber `0.00879`, validation Huber `0.05473`), indicating poor out-of-sample transfer compared to linear PCA-based ridge baselines (`Tx1 PCA8-ridge`), which achieve superior residual correlation (`0.133`) and lower validation error.

Sources: `docs/results/tx1_gmm_ridge_seed0/README.md:1-70`, `docs/results/tx1_gmm_ridge_seed0/evidence.json:1-176`

## Purpose and Scope
This leaf page documents the contents, provenance, and interpretation of the `docs/results/` hierarchy and related experimental archives within the codebase. It details verified empirical evidence from joint model runs (`docs/results/joint_geneeffect_seed0/`), stage-level diagnostic audits (`exp05`, `exp13`), prior internal evidence (`exp02`, `exp09`), baseline control evaluations (`Feng2024` profile baseline), and genetic-interaction coverage records (`Horlbeck 2018` K562 GI map).
